themselves (when copy-lint FAILs a word of it, the gate takes a waiver for that one hit with the brief
as the reason: `gate.md`). Selling on a sales page: persuasion is the genre; the test is whether it stands on facts.

# Copy voice

The copy layer. `copy.md` holds the rules every page keeps: the five rules, the contacts, nothing
invented. This file decides what the words say and how they sound, so two pages for two clients never
read like one writer. Read it at step 2, before the first sentence; `copy-tells.md` and
`scripts/copy-lint.mjs` check the result at step 6. The other three files: `copy-moves.md` (the move for
each part of the page), `copy-registers.md` (the voices to choose from), `copy-tells.md` (what gives
model copy away).

## Why model copy reads as model copy

The old slop is mostly gone: no "elevate", no "seamless", few em dashes. The new slop looks like good
copy, used the same way on every page:

- **One voice for every client:** warm, wry, modest, a little literary, mildly against big companies. A
  CI tool and a yoga studio sound alike.
- **The same devices in every section:** a strip of three invented figures, headings in two fragments
  ("Short menu. Long list of regulars."), "X, not Y", "No X. No Y.", a dry joke closing each paragraph, a
  pun signing off the footer.
- **Sincerity said instead of shown:** honest, calm, quiet, actually, simply, carefully.
- **Detail invented to look specific:** a batch number, a minute of the morning, a percentage nobody
  measured, and the same few names (Priya, Okafor, Fieldnote) on unrelated sites.

Professional copy uses the same devices. What separates it is five things: its details are **true**
(and often a little inconvenient); each device is used **once**, where it lands hardest; every brand has
its **own voice**; it takes **risks** (it names an enemy, admits a limit); and its pages are **uneven**,
leaving out what has nothing true to say. The cause underneath is missing input: with no facts, a model
fills a template with plausible inventions. **The fix is facts and decisions, never synonyms.** A word
swapped for its synonym is the next tell.

## 1. The fact sheet, from the brief

Before a sentence, write down what the brief, the client's files or an existing site give, word for
word where you can. Each field feeds a part of the page:

| Field | What it holds | Where it goes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| What it is | One plain sentence, no adjective | the h1 and the sub-line |
| For whom, and not for whom | The best-fit buyer; who should look elsewhere | the h1 or sub-line, one line in the FAQ |
| What they do today instead | A spreadsheet, the big rival, the bakery across town, nothing | the pain line, the comparison |
| The true difference | What is true here and not elsewhere, with its proof | the claims worth a heading |
| Customer words | Phrases from reviews, emails, the brief's own quotes | the pain line, headings |
| Numbers | Each with where it came from | sentences, the facts strip |
| People | Names and roles the brief gives | the about block, a quote |
| Odd true details | History, an object, a ritual, a house word, the awkward bit | the texture you would otherwise invent |
| A limit | What it does not do, who it is wrong for, what is closed | one admission a page |
| An enemy | A habit or a category ("re-typing invoices"), never the reader | the pain line, one section |
| The offer | Price, trial, booking terms, the one action | buttons, the close |

- **Nothing is invented** beyond what `copy.md` allows (a coined name; on a place, plausible hours and
  prices). An empty field stays empty: its section shrinks or goes, and the report lists what the client
  must supply. Never a `[NEED]`, a bracket or a "coming soon" on the page.
- **A thin brief is no reason to stop:** write the best page the facts allow. Only when a person is in
  the conversation and asks for copy (not a build) ask at most six questions in one message, most useful
  first: who switched to you from what, and why; the one number you would bet on; the objection you hear
  most; what you are bad at or not for; a strange true detail of how you work; three real customer
  messages.
- **A limit and an enemy come from the brief or from plain facts of the trade** ("closed Mondays",
  "Mac only", "no lift; rooms on three floors" when the brief says so). An invented flaw is still an
  invention.

## 2. The voice card

**The default voice is out** unless the client asks for it: warm, wry, modest, slightly literary,
ending paragraphs on a deadpan twist and saying honest, calm or quiet about itself. It is not bad; it is
what every model writes now, and readers know it.

Pick one register from `copy-registers.md` by the buyer, the price and the client's real character.
When the brief does not settle it, take the one least like the last page this session wrote. Write the
card on the plan (step 3), never on the page:

```
Voice: technical-dry (copy-registers.md 2)
Pairs: exact, not cold; sure, not loud; dry only in the empty state
Person: "you" for what the buyer gets, "we" for the work; the product is the subject in feature lines
Sentences: mostly 8 to 16 words; one long one a section, where it explains
Humour: none in the hero, the prices or the FAQ
House words: the brief's own nouns (shifts, rota, cover), the same word every time
Never: virtue words about ourselves, a pun on the name, a strip of claims
```

- **Copy the client's own voice first.** A writing sample, an old site or the brief's wording overrides
  the menu (never the five rules or the integrity rules).
- **Nine other trades:** picture this voice on nine businesses in nine other trades. If it suits any of
  them, push it further toward this client.
- **Voice holds, tone moves.** The hero and the story carry the most voice. Prices, the FAQ, booking and
  forms go plain: readers there are anxious. Errors and confirmations are short and kind.
- **The register never bends copy.md's rules:** the h1 still names the category, every heading still has
  its noun, every button is still a verb and an object (`copy.md`). Voice lives in which facts you pick,
  the sentence shapes, the admission and the microcopy.

## 3. Shape from the reader's questions

A reader asks, roughly in this order: what is this, is it for me, why believe you, how does it work,
what does it cost, what if it goes wrong, what do I do now. How much they already know sets the start:

- **They do not know they have the problem:** open the sub-line on a moment they recognise.
- **They know the problem:** name it in the customer's words, then the product.
- **They are comparing:** lead with the mechanism, what this does differently.
- **They know the client:** the product, the offer, the price, the action.

- **A section exists only if the brief has true material for it.** Five full sections beat eight
  padded ones; on a place, the photographs set the count (`sections.md`).
- **Counts follow the content:** four real features are four cards, one quote is one quote, two plans
  are two plans. Zero testimonials is a normal page.
- **Find the organising idea** when the brief has one: the menu as the page, a timetable, a founder's
  letter, one object carried through every section. Let it break the template once.
- **Not the skeleton:** eyebrow, claim heading, two-line lede, three cards, figures, in every section.
  Vary what goes in the sections: a list, a table, a short letter, one longer paragraph (five lines
  at most, `copy.md`), a heading with one line under it.

## 4. Draft

Read `copy-moves.md` before drafting a whole page.

- **Facts where adjectives want to go.** "Fast" is followed within the sentence by the figure or the
  mechanism; adjectives that stay are physical or measurable (wood-fired, 58 mm, ground-floor).
- **Proper nouns over categories:** the tools by name, the street, the river, the bus line.
- **The mechanism in verb-led steps.** How it works persuades more than how good it is.
- **The pain in the customer's words,** before the product, when the brief gives them.
- **One admission a page,** said plainly, from the brief.
- **Proof beside its claim,** from named outsiders the brief gives. No proof: a strip of plain facts
  from the brief, or nothing (`copy.md`).
- **Numbers in sentences, with their unit,** uneven where real.
- **Buttons:** a verb and the real object (`copy.md` rule 4). A true risk reversal sits beside the
  button ("Free for 14 days, no card"), only when the brief gives it.
- **Microcopy carries the voice too:** form labels and errors, the sent message, empty states, the 404
  page, the newsletter confirmation, a cookie notice if the page needs one. Write them in the register;
  this is where a dry line is welcome.
- **Sentence length follows meaning.** A short sentence lands a point; a long one carries an
  explanation. Not every line punchy; not variety by rule either.
- **Repeat the product's name** rather than cycling through "the platform, the tool, the solution".

## 5. The device budget, per page

None of these is banned; each works once. The problem is using them by default. `copy-lint.mjs`
counts them: over the budget is a WARN, twice the budget plus one or more is a FAIL (a tic).

| Device | Budget | Note |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Heading in two fragments "X. Y." | 1 | spend it where it lands hardest |
| Number-pair heading "Four X, one Y" | 0 to 1 | the most repeated model habit |
| Negation run "No X. No Y." | 1 | only when each item is a refusal a buyer can check |
| Contrast "X, not Y", isn't, rather than, instead of, without the | 2 in all | banning one form moves you to the next; count them together |
| Dry closing line on a paragraph | 2, never in a row | most paragraphs end on information |
| Pun on the name or its metaphor | 1, never the h1 | it is the page's one brand line (`copy.md` rule 3) |
| Sign-off line in the footer | 0 | the footer holds facts (`copy.md`) |
| Strip of figures | facts from the brief only | never invented KPIs |
| Virtue words about ourselves | 0 | the lint skips literal ones (a quiet room, calm water, genuine parts) and allows 2 |
| Lists of three | when there are three things | never in consecutive sentences |
| Step numbers on cards | only where the order is the content (a booking's steps) | none on features that read in any order |
| Eyebrow labels | 1 or 2 a page | a heading that names the thing needs none |
| Testimonials | the brief's only | name and role or town; none is fine |
| Response-time promise | 1, from the brief | the same words wherever it repeats |
| "Since [year]" | 1, from the brief | |

## 6. Check

At step 6, before the gate (which runs the lint again):

1. **Lint:** `node <skill>/scripts/copy-lint.mjs index.html --kind <kind>`. Fix every FAIL. Fix each
   WARN, or keep it on purpose and say why in the report.
2. **A rival's name:** put a rival's name, or the same trade in another town, into the h1, the sub-line
   and each heading. A line that still reads true says nothing about this client: rewrite it from the
   fact sheet.
3. **Sameness across pages:** when this session built other pages, pass them all to `copy-lint.mjs`
   at once and read the first headings side by side, and the heading phrases they share. A shared
   cadence or joke is a tic: break it.
4. **Read it aloud, as the client.** Cut every sentence they would not say about themselves.
5. **Over-correction:** after the fixes, look for the habit that replaced the one you removed: "rather
   than" multiplying, every sentence a fragment, everything in pairs, a joke deleted and nothing in its
   place. A rule that made a sentence worse is broken on purpose.
6. **A fresh reader,** when the run can spare a subagent: give it only the page's text and ask what
   this is, who it is for, why this over the alternative, what it costs, what would make it hesitate,
   and which three lines sound like any other website. Fix what it finds. Never iterate to beat an AI
   detector.

The report carries the voice card in one line, every assumed price or hour (`copy.md`), and what the
client must supply.

# Copy Say what it is and what it does, in words a stranger understands in five seconds. Every sentence is one you would say out loud to a customer. No metaphors, poetry, invented terms or ad wording (the one brand line of rule 3 aside). Every studied site is a description only: copy how the examples are written (plain, category first), never their words, code, pictures or signature effect. ## The copy layer This file holds the rules every page keeps. What the words say and how they sound is the copy layer, read at step 2 before the first sentence: - `copy-voice.md`: the fact sheet from the brief, the voice card, the page's shape from the reader's questions, the device budget, the checks. Start here. - `copy-registers.md`: the voices to choose from, and which suit which trade. - `copy-moves.md`: the move for each part of the page: hero forms that name the category, headings, the story, features, proof, prices, buttons, microcopy, the footer. - `copy-tells.md`: what gives model copy away and the fix for each, what over-correction breeds, and what is not a tell. Where they differ, this file wins: nothing invented, nothing bracketed or left open on the page, no captions, the h1 names the category, buttons are a verb and an object. **copy-lint.** `node /scripts/copy-lint.mjs index.html --kind ` counts the countable tells in well under a second a page (no browser). FAIL: residue (a `[NEED]`, a template token, markdown, chatbot lines), the old slop words and stock lines, and a device used more than twice its budget plus one (three two-fragment headings, five contrast frames, five virtue words): fix every one. WARN: a device over its budget, a strip of figures, a default-cast name, a footer sign-off, a response-time promise worded twice, proof figures, exclamation marks, puffery, a stale year: fix it or keep it and say why in the report. Several pages at once also print their first headings side by side and the heading phrases they share. `--json` for scripts; exit 1 on a FAIL. The gate runs it on the page as a static check: its FAILs block like the checker's (ids `copy-*`), its WARNs do not. ## Five rules 1. **The h1 names the category, and for a brand nobody knows, the buyer or the place,** in 2 to 8 words: payroll app, dental clinic, standing desk, plus who it is for or where. A place: what and where in 40 characters at most ("Bakery on Mill Street, Leith"; "Six-room guesthouse on a fjord"). A game: its name and genre ("Kelpmoor, a co-op sailing game"), or its wordmark over an h1 naming the genre; the launch date or status the brief gives is the hard fact. Never a riddle, a command, a mood, or a brand line over a plain sub-line. 2. **The first screen holds one hard fact:** a number, a place, a price or a date. 3. **Every heading has a noun that names a thing:** the product, a part of it, the place, a section noun (prices, rooms, menu, opening hours, questions, getting here, visit) or a digit. One brand line a page at most, never the h1: it is the page's one figure of speech or pun, with a fact in the line under it. 4. **Buttons are a verb plus what the visitor gets,** 1 to 5 words, starting with book, buy, order, pre-order, reserve, try, start, get, download, compare, see, watch, read, find, join, subscribe, sign up, contact, configure, add, send, email or request; a bare noun only where the link opens that thing. Never "Learn more", "Read more", "Discover", "Explore", "More" or "Click here". 5. **Few actions, each with one wording:** at most 2 in the hero (one on a place), 10 different labels a page at most. The main action names the transaction (Book a room, Order a cake, Start a free trial; on a place the brief's order or booking, else Get directions, never a side event) and reads the same in the nav, the hero, the close and the phone bar, and nowhere else. One screen shows it twice at most: the nav's button and the hero's on a desktop (the checker WARNs it, so look that nothing else repeats it), the hero's on a phone (system.js keeps the phone bar away from a screen that already shows its action); a third copy on one screen FAILs [action-repeat]. ## Plain versions When a line is vague: the category noun first, then one count, place or price from the brief, no figure of speech. | Vague | Plain | | --- | --- | | "Every shift, sorted" | Shift planning for restaurant teams | | "Where the city climbs" | Climbing gym with 180 routes in Leipzig-Plagwitz | | "Come climb" | Day pass 14 €, shoes included | | "A second read of every word" | AI proofreader for book publishers | ## Headlines and text - **Hero sub-line:** software, product and service: how it works and the main benefit, 15 to 30 words, one line to two sentences. A place: the fact, 80 characters at most, with today's hours ("Sourdough, rye and cardamom buns from 7:30, Tuesday to Sunday."); a hotel the rooms and the town. - **Section headings** name the thing ("Rooms and prices", "Works with your tools") or make a short plain claim ("Pays staff on the same day"), 1 to 6 words, at most two lines. A noun phrase, "we do X for Y", or a verb with the thing it acts on ("Send invoices from the van"); never a bare command ("Get started", "Come climb"), a question (FAQ entries may be questions), a colon heading or a line that only makes sense after the page ("Continuity slips", "It reads everything you decide"). Two fragments ("Twelve rooms. Three ways to stay.") once a page at most (`copy-tells.md`). **Card titles:** a verb and an object ("Warns about double shifts"), one line, real words, never a coy label ("The market run"). A heading with a grey second half is two sentences: the first ends with a full stop before the `.muted` span ("Rooms and prices. Breakfast included."), never two phrases that run into one [run-on]. - **Under a heading** one line to two sentences (10 to 40 words); a card body 1 or 2 sentences, 25 words at most, in the buyer's words with one concrete detail; no paragraph over five lines at 1440. A price does the selling, not a mood heading ("Rooms from 140 € a night, breakfast included"). - **Words per screen** stay low: product 47, place 44, service 34; a page about 900 words at most, the footer aside. Long copy goes to sub-pages. - **The tech word budget** (software, gaming, hardware): 60 to 80 words a screen at 1440, counted outside UI mocks, diagrams and code (headings, lines, card titles and bodies, buttons, labels); over 80 the checker WARNs (in testing: a fintech page at 117 words a screen read as wordy). Cut in this order: a second sentence under a heading, card bodies to one sentence of 12 to 18 words, a fourth card, a list a fragment already shows. The UI says the rest. - **Numbers** sit in sentences with their unit ("4.5 hours a week"), uneven where real (212, 38%). A real claim from the brief that needs a source gets a numbered footnote near the footer (13px and up). - **Pictures** stand beside short copy, never in place of it, and words never stand where a photograph fits. Every word is live text. - **Form words:** a label says what goes in ("Arrival", "Guests"), never a question or a placeholder in its place; an error names the field and what to type ("Write the day you want to come"); the sent line names what was sent in the button's own words ("Your table request is in. We reply within a day."). The rest of the recipe: `system.md`, Forms. - **Self-check:** read each line aloud to a customer. Is it clear what the product does? If not, rewrite it. Then the copy layer's checks (`copy-voice.md` section 6), copy-lint first. ## What may be assumed - **Prices, address, hours and dates come from the brief;** the report lists any you assumed. Only two things may be assumed when the brief lacks them: a coined brand name (below), and on a place plausible hours and prices for the trade, uneven and in the local currency (3.60, not 4.00). Nothing else is invented: a product or service with no price in the brief says "Price on request" or shows none. Each assumed price, hour, date or place carries `data-assumed` on its own element (`3.60 €`, `
`); the checker lists every one for the report [assumed], and assumed hours never drive an open-now line [open-now]. - **No invented proof:** no invented reviews, ratings, review counts, quotes, testimonials, statistics, customer counts, customer names, portraits, clients, awards, press lines or products. Customer logos only for real customers the brief names and that may be shown; a real tool the product works with keeps its real icon in its own colours (`icons.md`), never a drawn imitation. Without proof, a strip of plain facts from the brief, or nothing. - **No sample notes:** no "sample", "(sample)", "examples", "illustrative" tag, note or asterisk footnote anywhere. A target value the brief itself gives is worded inside it ("target 2 days"). - **No placeholders:** no square brackets, "lorem ipsum", "your name here", "to be added", TODO, kit sample text, and no link to `#` or an empty href. Write the real words, or leave the element out. "Coming soon" only for what the brief says is coming. - **No caption, label or description under or on any visual** (house rule): not "A drawing made in code", "Photographs follow", "Representative image", not a name, price or link line under a bare picture, no hashtags. A heading names the set; a sold item's name and price sit inside its card's padding. The picture shows the thing or is left out; the report lists the photographs the client must supply. - **Credits:** one short line at the end of the footer naming only the sources used, never the photographers: "Photographs via Unsplash and Wikimedia Commons" (as `photos.mjs credits` prints it; 110 characters at most, one line from 1024) that links or opens the credits list. Paste the line and the list exactly as `photos.mjs credits` prints them; never write a credit link per photograph into the footer (in testing: 18 and 20 credit links in a footer read as a credit wall). Map data credits join it. A page that shows real logos adds "Product names and logos are trademarks of their owners". - **Each fact once:** an opening time, a price or an address has one value and one wording, repeated word for word only where it belongs (the hero, the visit panel, the phone sheet, the close, the footer); never two hours for one day. ## Contacts the brief does not give What the brief gives is printed exactly as given. Each kind is separate: a brief that gives only a phone number still gets the address, email and imprint rules. - **Address: a street and a district only** ("Elmgatan, Malmö-Möllevången"). Never a house number, a postcode or map coordinates. One street address a page (the visit block and the footer, at 390 too), never readable only on a sign in a photograph. Several shops: each name, then its street. A studio by appointment says so. - **A brief with no street:** print the district only ("Eimsbüttel, Hamburg"), the town when no district is named, and never an invented street or number; the type moment `address` sets that district. List the missing street in the report as the client's to supply. - **Maps:** no map loads with the page. Get directions opens `https://www.openstreetmap.org/search?query=+`, with no coordinates and no route; on the phone the address opens the same search. No street given: the link says "See the area" and opens `?query=+`; only a town: no map link and no directions button at all, since a search for a whole city shows nobody the door [map-link]. A map is drawn only for a street the brief gives (`fx-map` baked still, the pin on the street line, never a building); a builder's real street never gets a real map, since it pins a stranger's door. Never an iframe. - **Phone: none, unless the brief gives one.** No number, no `tel:` link, no Call button. A "Request a call" form may stand in. - **No imprint page and no company details:** no register number (HRB), VAT or tax id, company number, managing director or court. The legal row holds the brand, the current year, Privacy, Terms and the credits line; an Imprint link only when the brief gives the company's own details. - **Email and web:** a form (`system.md`, Forms: it posts to the client's form address when the brief gives one, else its `mailto:` on `.example` stands in and the report lists it), or a button ("Email us") whose `mailto:` is on `.example` (`hello@brand.example`). Never print an email address, a domain or a social handle, not even a `.example` one. `.socials` stays empty unless the brief gives the accounts. - **Names are coined,** not dictionary words and not a business that exists, unless the brief gives the name, and never one that models keep coining (Kestrel, Halcyon, Lumen, Nimbus, Fieldnote: `copy-tells.md`; copy-lint FAILs one as the page's own name, in its title or h1, and WARNs one anywhere else, a logo wall or a mock); person names come only from the brief. Search a coined name with its trade ("name coffee") and as a domain; if a business of that trade or a famous person has that exact name in the first 10 results, coin another. Write each query and result in `names.json` beside the page (`"searched": false` with no search tool). - **Links** go where their label says: a part of the page (`#rooms`) or a page that exists; never "here", never two different labels to one target, never a link to a closed answer. - **Newsletter:** asked once, in or just above the footer, "Subscribe" or "Sign up", an email field only; never in a modal, never twice. ## Banned Metaphors and "where X meets Y"; slogans, greetings and boasts in the hero; questions as headlines; exclamation marks; all-caps labels; invented capitalised concepts ("the Proof Layer"); unexplained programme names; jokes or slang in labels; mood paragraphs; a literary quote as a full-screen band; filler (seamless, effortless, cutting-edge, unlock, elevate, supercharge, reimagine, next-generation, game-changing, powerful, robust, and the rest of `copy-tells.md`); virtue words about the client (honest, calm, quiet, actually, simply); a sign-off or a pun in the footer; the model's default voice (`copy-voice.md` section 2). copy-lint FAILs the old slop words, the stock phrases, left residue and a device used past twice its budget; it WARNs the rest it can count, and the rival's-name check and the read-aloud (`copy-voice.md` section 6) catch what it cannot.

``` A spec that does not parse logs a `console.error` and leaves only the names it could read. ## The builder page (the tool for building one fast) Open `assets/diagrams/lab.html` over http. Pick a page kind and a preset, edit the JSON (it redraws while you type) or use the controls (ground, light, line shape, cycle 2.5 to 4 s), switch card, section, phone and light, dark, restart the loop, then copy the markup and the icon line. Inside a card it shows the real thing, never a mock-up. A new diagram is a preset plus the client's words; `free` takes nodes at fractions of the box and the edges you list. ## Icons: one resolver, run it last `diagram.js` reads icon files and nothing else: no CDN, no tinting, no Simple Icons call at runtime. From the site root: `node /scripts/icons.mjs scan index.html --out assets/icons` fetches every id the page's diagrams name (curated short names such as `gmail`, `steam`, `google-docs`; `logos:`, `file:`, `si:` ids; `ui:` glyphs). Colour marks come from the logos set in full colour; where none exists (Google Docs, Sheets, Slides) the Simple Icons mark in its brand hex, painted by `icons.mjs`. An icon that is missing shows the name's first letter, and the console says `diagram.js: N icons are not in .../assets/icons ...` with the fetch line: run it. A finished page has no such line. Marks that are mostly violet (Stripe, Twitch) are drawn in the text colour, black marks take the ink, a wordmark gets a 2:1 slot and its tile becomes a pill: all decided by `icons.mjs` and baked into the file (`data-ic`). `data-icon-base` on the element or around it moves the folder. ## Motion: one cycle of 2.5 to 4 s - A diagram card's pulse is its own loop (not one per card group). The program is laid out as a ripple: each spoke, branch or route starts a beat after the one before it (0.24 to 0.5 s, the stagger), and the whole program is then fitted to ONE cycle of 3.2 s (`"motion": {"cycle": 2.5..4}`), the lines fading in the rest. `d.T` is always 2.5 to 4 s. It repeats. Below the hero two loops never share a screen: beside a looping fragment one of the two holds (`motion.md`). - It restarts from its first beat when the pointer enters the card (mouse and pen) or focus moves into it by keyboard. - It runs only on screen. On a phone (under 640px) and under reduced motion it holds one still, the busiest moment; `"pulse": "none"` holds it too. `data-dg-still` holds it by hand and plays it while the pointer is on the card. `data-ui-still` does not hold a diagram. A loop that runs gets the pause disc. - The light is a gradient comet with a glow and a bright head (`"pulse": "dot"` is the head alone). Size: a flat drawing takes the next size up when that fits; `"size": "band"` or `"card"` forces it. - Lines: hub spokes are straight rays from the core's rim (`"curve": "curve"`, `"elbow"` or `"swirl"` change them); flows bend in rounded elbows. ## Labels plain - A tool by its name (Gmail, Zendesk), a step by its result (Reply drafted, Label printed), a place by its city. One to three words. - Real-looking numbers in `meta` (2,481, 14 ms). - No jargon nodes ("Orchestration layer", "AI engine"): the core is called what the product calls it. - Up to 8 spokes, up to 12 nodes in a card. Crowded means it should be a list. - No caption under the diagram. The card title says what it shows; `alt` in the spec says it for screen readers. - Tool marks in their own colours, never a letter in a circle. A core without an icon is a pill with its name.

# Effects beyond backgrounds

An effect can be a part of the page, not only its ground: the picture in a feature card, a real object
drawn in dither, the letters of a headline, a button's fill, a border, an icon chip, a chart's area, a
map. The parts are in `assets/components/` (a folder each: `component.html`, `.css`, `.js`,
`meta.json`); `index.html` there shows them live with a palette switcher, starting each part only
while it is near the screen.

**Tech pages only** (site-kind software, gaming or tech: hardware), except `fx-photo` (every kind, as
a plain photograph) and `fx-map` (every kind with a door, a place included, baked still, and only
for a street the brief gives). What each kind may carry: `effects-usage.md`. `fx-band` is out: a
drawn band between sections is not a section. `fx-logos` is out: real logos show in their full
colours and never move (rule 7, MO-57; `sections-library.md` logo-row).

## Under the one-effect rule

- **Every part that holds a WebGL context is the page's one effect** (`effects-usage.md`): the
  dither object, a filled headline or stat, the globe, the avatar ring, the logo light, the progress
  light, the prompt glow, the edge-glow plan, `fx-spotlight`, and `fx-button`'s fill (on the one
  primary call to action, or one pair, fading in on hover or focus). It sits in the hero or the one
  `[data-visual]` frame, or serves a dealt moment in its own section; never beside a live hero
  ground. Painted panels in a 2x2 are card grounds drawn still, not the effect.
- **One pointer effect a page:** `fx-button`, `fx-spotlight`, a turning object, or a hover or liquid
  moment (`moments.md`), never two. The street map and a photograph are content, not effects.
- Everything else stays **quiet**: a search glow only while focused, one ring on the recommended
  plan, chips with a still grain. **One lit border a page** (`fx-prompt` or `fx-pricing`).
- A glow only on a dark ground, once, behind the key object in the hero or `[data-visual]`, still,
  never spilling onto text or round a button. One-shot transitions (a tile flip, a melt, a crack)
  only once, on a click or as a hero reveal, inside the `[data-visual]`; scroll-driven only as a
  dealt section moment. Ray marching only in a dark hero, at half resolution; halftone and dither
  only as a still ground, never on a photograph.
- Nothing moves with scroll; a card never moves by itself. Motion lives inside a visual: a pointer
  clicking in a UI window, rotors that spin up under the pointer, a seat that swivels after it.

## Cost: light enough for a laptop's integrated GPU

A laptop's graphics chip shares about 2 GB with everything else; too many live canvases crash it.

- **At most 4 live WebGL contexts per page** (house rule; `perf.md`), and only for things that move: the
  one effect and a dealt moment's own canvas. Everything still holds none at rest.
- **Stills render once.** An effect that does not move (speed and drift 0) goes through `still()` in
  `shared.js` (or `fill(el, id, { still: true })` for type): drawn once as it nears the screen,
  copied into a plain picture, its context freed. Stills draw one after another, so they never hold
  more than one context at a time. Never leave a still effect mounted with its frame loop running,
  and never give a still to a pause button (Play would start its loop).
- **Screenshots wait for the stills.** On a CPU renderer each still takes about a second (a new
  context, its shader compiled, one frame), so a screen captured a fixed time after a scroll catches
  some blank and a panel cut by two screens comes out half lit. While stills near the screen have no
  picture yet, `<html data-cx-baking="n">` says how many. A screenshot must wait until it is gone;
  `shoot.mjs` and `consistency.mjs` do not wait on it yet, so shoot a page with stills (filled stats,
  type in an effect, painted panels) with `--wait 1500` and look for unfilled digits before judging.
- **Per-pixel and raymarched work at 1 sample per CSS pixel at most** (0.75 when the canvas is large)
  and about 1.5 megapixels at most, whatever the screen's DPR. `fx-dither-object` runs once per
  dither cell (a ninth of the CSS pixels); `painterly-landscape` at 0.6.
- **Everything pauses** off screen and in a hidden tab (fx.js does it for every mounted effect), and
  a loop that runs on its own for more than about 5 s has a pause button.
- What holds a context on a page: `fx-dither-object` (20 fps), `fx-prompt`, `fx-globe`, `fx-avatar`
  and `fx-progress`, each only while near the screen; `fx-button` only while
  pointed at (freed 4 s later), `fx-search` only while focused. A page carries one of these (the
  effect). Every other part is a still, and so is the dither object under reduced motion. `fx-map`
  (plain SVG) and `fx-photo` (the photograph itself) hold no context at all.

## Feature cards with inset panels (`fx-feature-card`)

The card reviewers point at, as x.ai and Figma build it: a 2x2 of cards, each a title and two grey lines,
then an inset panel with its own 8px margin (radius = card radius - margin). The panel holds a bright
ground and one UI window that runs out through the panel's bottom edge.

- Ground: `painterly-landscape` (default) or `grain-gradient`, still, drawn once as pictures (the
  cards hold no context at rest).
- A landscape is a picture, so it takes a natural light near the page, never one hue over everything.
  Each panel names its light in `data-cx-scene` and its composition in `data-cx-params` (horizon,
  side, slope), so no two panels look alike:
  - `day`: a pale sky over hills that step down to a near slope; graphite hills under a warm accent,
    blue-grey under a cool one, the accent itself when it is green or neutral, deeper shades of the
    page colour on a colour page.
  - `dusk`: an evening as it looks: a deep blue sky that lights up in gold only along the horizon,
    dark hills with a lit crest, whatever the accent (a blue glow under a blue accent read as the
    `day` panel again, only darker); the gold leans toward a warm accent but stays between amber and
    gold (red-orange turns the crests rust). On a colour page, a light shade of the page colour.
  - `meadow`: daylight as a photograph shows it, whatever the page: a clear blue sky paling to the
    horizon, a blue far ridge, a sunlit field of grass (on a blue colour page the sky is the page colour).
    The natural picture among the panels, as on x.ai's cards; one per grid.
  - A grid of four mixes them: for example `day`, a grain, `dusk`, `meadow`.
- A grain panel: a light warm ground under a warm accent, a deep one under a cool accent, the page
  colour's own shades on a colour page.
- The window shows the feature with real labels: an invoice, a checkout, a list of payouts, an invite.
  Its content runs out through the panel's bottom edge: no empty space under the last row.
- Two panels at most run a short pointer demo (glide, click, the state changes, rest), one per row.
- Rejected: a small dialog centred on an empty ground; an orb or sphere ground; a landscape painted in
  the accent's hue only (it reads as a filter, and an orange accent turns rust-red); a warm accent mixed
  into a dark ground or a complementary accent mixed into a colour page (mud).

## Objects in dither (`fx-dither-object`)

A real thing built in code as a lit 3D form and printed in ordered dither in the page tones: ground,
shade, ink, accent and a deep accent. Use it when the product has no photograph yet, as the hero
picture or the visual of one split section.

- Objects: `headphones` (over-ear, on their cups), `chair` (an office chair on five castors),
  `camera` (a mirrorless camera with a zoom lens), `drone` (a camera drone with four rotors). Set
  `data-cx-object` on the figure.
- Idle: it sways slowly on its spot. Pointed at, it turns to the pointer, the light comes from the
  pointer, and it answers with its own working part: sound rings out of the cups, the seat swivels
  after the pointer (the base stays), the lens zooms out as the pointer rises and its focus ring
  turns, the rotors spin up into discs and the drone lifts off its legs and tips toward the pointer.
- The accent paints one part: the ear cups, the seat and back, the camera's body band and shutter,
  the drone's shell; their shaded side is a deep accent, never grey.
- Only an object the product really is or sells, on a tech page (a drone, a camera, headphones as
  hardware). One per page, with no caption under the stage: the section
  heading or copy says what it is and gives one real fact from the client.
- A product none of the four fits gets its own photographs or a render from `assets/objects`, never
  the nearest of these four and never mood stock in its place.
- The print is the render to use. `data-cx-render="studio"` (the same form as a smooth shaded render)
  is not for pages yet: at one sample per CSS pixel its edges stair-step, and next to a real product
  shot its forms read as toys. Never pick it for a shop or a product page; use the print, or the
  client's own photographs.
- Under reduced motion it is one still picture with no context and no pause button; without WebGL a
  line drawing of the same object, its accent part filled.
- It is a drawing of the product, never a filter: no photograph is ever dithered, halftoned or
  printed (in testing: a halftone over the hero photograph read as broken and low-res at every width).

## Street map of the place (`fx-map`)

A visit or contact section shows the real streets around the place, as a map app would, in the page's
colours: the judges marked a contour pattern standing in for a map as a fake drawing.

- **Bake once** at build time: `node assets/components/fx-map/bake.mjs --lat <lat> --lon <lon> --out
  map.json` fetches the streets, water, parks, rails and stations from OpenStreetMap (one request to
  an Overpass server) and writes a small JSON (about 55 KB, 18 KB gzipped, for 3 x 2 km of a city):
  streets in four classes, water (the sea built from coastlines too), parks, rails and trams, up to
  14 street names placed along the straightest part of each street. `--from none` (the default) leaves
  the walk out; only on a tech page whose brief names a station, `--from auto` (the nearest station
  150 m to 1.6 km away) or `--from lat,lon --from-name` adds the walk with its minutes at 80 m a minute. Paste the JSON inline
  (`<script type="application/json" class="cx-map__data">`) or name the file in `data-cx-map`.
- The part fits the pin, the walk and both names into the free part of the frame (right of the card
  from 900px of width; under 900px the card sits below and the map keeps the whole width), never
  closer than about 1 m a pixel; names go on the side the walk does not leave by (above or below on a
  phone). Street names show only where they fit their street and clear every other label.
- Light pages: white streets with a hairline casing on a land one step darker than the page. Dark
  pages: lighter streets on a land one step lighter. Water and parks keep a natural blue and green
  mixed into the land (natural colour, like the `meadow` landscape).
- Pointed at, or its directions link focused, the walk is drawn from the station to the door and the
  pin's halo answers once. Nothing moves at rest or on scroll.
- Drawn only for a street the brief gives; the pin sits on the street line, never on a building;
  the card says the walk in words ("5 minutes on foot from The Shore tram stop") and names street and
  district only (`copy.md`, Contacts). Get directions opens
  `https://www.openstreetmap.org/search?query=<street>+<district>`, never coordinates or a route
  link. On a place, and on any other page of kind other, it is baked with `--from none` (no walk, no
  minutes chip) and nothing moves. The coordinates go only to the bake, never onto the page. The
  OpenStreetMap credit ("Map data © OpenStreetMap contributors") joins the footer's one credits line,
  never on or under the map.
- No network at build time, or a street the brief does not give: no map; the visit shows its
  photograph. Never ship a contour or dot fallback as a map.

## A photograph with copy (`fx-photo`)

- The client's photograph in its natural colour, the copy on its calm, dark corner (white type, no
  scrim), as figma.com and x.ai show theirs; in a link it zooms 1.02 to 1.03 inside its frame
  (`motion.md`). Words on a photograph only in the hero and one band a page, never on a place.
- No filter over it: no halftone, dither, dissolve, print, duotone or blur (`data-cx-grade` stays
  off).
- The photographer's credit goes in the page's one footer credit line, never under the picture.
- It takes no dealt effect: its `effects` list is empty on purpose and `data-cx-effect` is ignored.
  No WebGL and nothing at rest; under reduced motion the zoom is off.

## The techniques (`components/shared.js`)

- `still(el, id)`: an effect that does not move, drawn once and kept as a picture (see Cost).
- `fill(el, id)`: the glyphs of `el` (or its `[data-fill]` parts) show the effect. The overlay sits
  next to `el`, never inside it, so the text and HTML stay clean. `{ still: true }` for a still fill.
- `windows(host, targets)`: one canvas seen through many shapes (chips, bars, cards).
- `cx-ring`: a host shown only in its padding, a 1.5px border of the effect.
- `cx-glow`: a host blurred into a soft light behind one object.
- `pauser(host)`: a round pause button in one corner of a looping visual. **Every loop that runs on
  its own for more than about 5 s gets one** (WCAG 2.2.2): the panel demos, the dither object, the
  prompt glow, the globe, the logo light, the call preview, the import preview. Under reduced motion
  the loops hold one state and the button is hidden. Stills (the map, the band) need none.

## When to use each

| Part | Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|---|
| `fx-feature-card` | A 2x2 of product features | Features with nothing to show in a window |
| `fx-dither-object` | The product as an object, with no photograph (the print render) | Decoration that is not the product; a studio render |
| `fx-headline` | The hero line or closing line; fill 2-3 words | Body text, two filled lines on a page |
| `fx-stat` | 2-4 proof numbers from the brief, at the stat size (`--t-stat`, 38 at 1440) | Small numbers, count-ups, invented figures |
| `fx-button` | The one primary call to action | Every button |
| `fx-prompt` | The hero prompt box of an AI or dev product | Ordinary forms |
| `fx-search` | Docs or command search | A field that always glows |
| `fx-tabs` | A product tour or dashboard preview | Navigation |
| `fx-icon-tiles` | A feature grid with drawn glyphs | Brand logos |
| `fx-spotlight` | A row of plain feature cards (security, admin) | A page with another pointer effect |
| `fx-globe` | Products with global reach | Local businesses |
| `fx-map` | Visit or contact: the real streets around the door, baked still | A product without a place |
| `fx-chart` | One metric over time | Decoration without numbers |
| `fx-bars` | Monthly figures on a labelled scale | More than 16 bars |
| `fx-photo` | The client's own photograph of the subject, in colour | Mood stock, blank notebooks, filters |
| `fx-avatar` | Calls, presence, a team list | Static team grids |
| `fx-pricing` | The recommended plan | All plans |
| `fx-progress` | Only inside a product window, as its own import or setup step (a UI fragment) | A progress bar as a card or visual of its own (the judge marks it); page loaders |

## Picking the effect

- **Panels in feature cards:** `painterly-landscape` (with a scene), `grain-gradient`;
  `ruled-grounds` for a technical product's panel that holds no UI (never behind a window or fragment, `cards.md`).
- **Inside letters and digits:** `silk-folds`, `aurora-curtains` (dark and colour pages), still. On a
  light page, stat digits get a plain ink fade instead (an effect in digits on white reads as scratched
  metal). Never `fluted-glass` in type: on a colour ground it paints thick accent bars through the
  letters. Never `caustics`, `halftone-screen` or `line-engraving` in type.
- **Inside small shapes** (chips, pills, bars): `grain-gradient` with still grain, low contrast. No
  silk, glass or metal sheen in a pill or a bar.
- **Inside data:** a plain accent fade under a line (the chart default) or a still `ruled-grounds`;
  bars take a still, low-contrast `grain-gradient`. Never an effect that draws its own grid or moving
  traces over a chart, and never `halftone-screen` in a chart area (its tone runs across the frame,
  so half the area goes empty).
- **A map** (`fx-map`) is the baked streets, never an effect, and has no fallback ground.
- Each part keeps a table of params per effect it takes and passes only that effect's own: one
  effect's numbers mean something else to another (contour-lines' opacity 0.32 and calm 0.55 left
  dot-terrain almost blank).
- **A button's fill:** an even, low-contrast grain that moves only while pointed at; no blobs that
  settle at one end of the button.
- When the page's deal gives an effect listed in a part's `meta.json` `effects`, use it there
  (`data-cx-effect`, `data-cx-fill` for type); otherwise its `default`. A part with an empty list
  (`fx-photo`, `fx-dither-object`) takes no dealt effect: a photograph is never filtered.
- Retired effects (`marble-warp`, `truchet-arcs`, `pixel-mosaic` and the others listed in
  `assets/effects/README.md`) are in no part's list. `grid-pulse` stays out of charts: its traces
  blink at random.

## Colour

Every part reads the page tokens. `inkPalette` draws an effect as ink (pale on dark pages, deep on
light ones); `accentPalette` keeps it near the accent with the label at 4.5:1; `tone(p, k)` matches
the CSS card steps. No fixed hues, with three exceptions, all natural colour as a photograph or a map
app would show it: the `meadow` landscape (a blue sky over grass), the gold horizon of `dusk` (the
other landscapes are built from the page's own hues and greys), and the map's water and parks (a blue
and a green mixed into the land). Never violet or lavender.

the stand-in photograph with the client's own; a figure the brief does not give is left out, never
invented and never tagged "sample" (`copy.md`).

# Effects usage

Who gets effects, how many, how they are dealt and where they sit. An effect is anything a shader,
canvas, WebGL, a print pass or a scroll drive makes: effect grounds (`data-fx`, `assets/effects`),
the WebGL creative parts (`effects-creative.md`), objects and prints (`effects-objects.md`), big
scenes (`scenes.md`), the tech moments (`moments.md`; the photo- and type-led ones every kind deals
are not effects), a film or 3D hero and timed loops. `cards.md` wins on
any card detail; `motion.md` holds every timing.

## The gate (house rule 8)

Effects are for site-kind tech, software and gaming (AI and developer tools count as software) and
for a product page with a technical subject (hardware, devices). Never on a place, an ordinary
product brand or shop, a service firm, an agency or a studio: they are site-kind other.

On other, photographs, type and flat colour carry the page. Banned there: canvas and WebGL, autoplay
video, any CSS gradient (grounds, panels, glows, scrims), SVG pattern or texture grounds,
`backdrop-filter` (the nav too), `filter`, `mix-blend-mode`, `mask-image`, glass, grain, halftone,
dither, duotone, print, `[data-fx]`, `[data-print]`, `[data-scene]`, `[data-big-scene]`,
`[data-ui-loop]`, `[data-m-loop]`, `[data-m-count]`, SVG animation, GIFs, Lottie, a
custom cursor and any scroll or animation library. Allowed: the hero's entrance and the one or two
dealt photo- or type-led moments (`photo-chapters`, `pinned-chapters`, `picture-develops` in its
film look, `word-highlight`: `moments.md`), `fx-map` baked still, `fx-photo` as a
plain photograph, real icons, a still diagram (not on a place), and on a physical product whose
brief asks for 3D its own product render (`[data-product]`, `effects-objects.md`): the product's
picture, not an effect: stills by default, live only when asked (`data-product-mode="live"`), at
most one live context, on the flat ground, its poster beneath. Without that ask a product with no
photographs is shown in stand-in photographs (`photos.md`).
