| The one effect | a live ground, a WebGL part, an object or a big scene | none | none |
| Card panel grounds | one card group, still, from the effect's family; with a big scene the lit ground (`data-ground`), no `data-fx` | the client's photograph | none |
| Moments | 1 or 2 a page, two at most in all: in sections, one of them may sit in the hero | 1 or 2 in sections, photo- or type-led (`moments.md`) | 1 or 2 in sections, photo- or type-led (`moments.md`) |
| Big scene | 0 or 1 (it is the effect) | none | none |
| Diagram cards | 0 to 2, pulsing | 0 or 1, still | none |
| Loops | one timed loop, one per card group | none | none |
| CSS grounds | 0 to 2 (`backgrounds.md`) | flat tokens | flat tokens |

**The subject before the effect** (in testing: a robot arm shown as a silk shader and an order form,
and an unnamed game shown as an abstract effect, both lost to pages that showed the thing). An
effect never stands where the product, the device or the game's world should be. Hardware with no
photographs or client renders takes stand-in photographs of the same kind of machine at work, and
a game with no art files its name set large over stand-in photographs of its setting (`photos.md`,
Live search; `sections.md`, Product and Gaming), full bleed in the world section. When the brief
asks for 3D, a product render (`effects-objects.md`, Product renders) is the picture instead, not
the effect: the page's one effect may sit behind it as the stage's ground (every render placement
is transparent over its frame), counts as the beat and shares the four contexts with it; it never
replaces the picture and never sits beside it as a second focal visual.

Every visual that is not the effect, a card ground, a moment, the scene or a product render is a
real UI capture or a real photograph. A photograph is never filtered, printed, dithered or graded on any page.

## Tech budget

- **One effect:** one live ground (the hero ground, or a ground inside the one framed
  `[data-visual]` window under an h2), or one WebGL part (an `fx-*` that holds a context: the button
  fill, a search or prompt glow, the edge-glow plan, spotlight, globe, avatar, logos, progress,
  dither object, filled headline or stat), or one object, or one big scene. A grain, dither or
  texture CSS ground counts as it. Never in a fixed layer, never behind body copy, never a
  page-long canvas; a 3D world lives in the hero only.
- **Card grounds** (house rule: "gradients and effects ... as a card's background with a smaller
  card of text or UI on top"): one card group may hold quiet grounds from the effect's family,
  drawn once and held as pictures (system.js frees their contexts); not a second live effect. With
  a big scene there is no `data-fx` outside a moment (the checker FAILs it, MO-16, MO-23): the card
  panels take the lit ground (`data-ground`).
- **Moments** (house rule): up to two section moments that may follow the scroll (letters, liquid,
  a section transition, a counter, a marquee row), each in its own section, and at most one
  non-scroll moment (load, hover or click) in the hero or `[data-visual]`, never in or beside the
  scene's section; two moments in all at most. A moment built as an `fx` part carries its own `data-fx` id on its
  own section; it is not a second ground.
- **Beats:** the effect, the scene and the moments are the page's beats, up to three on tech. Name
  each and its section in the plan; never two in one section or in neighbouring sections; a calm
  section between them; the back third of the page calm before the close. CSS grounds, card
  grounds, diagrams, card loops and hovers are not beats.
- **One pointer effect** a page: a hover or liquid moment, `fx-button`, `fx-spotlight` or an object
  that turns to the pointer, never two. Never a replaced cursor, never a magnetic button.
- **At most four live WebGL contexts** at once (house rule): the effect plus the moments' own canvases;
  `perf.mjs` fails above four.

## Deal the effect, never by taste

`node <skill>/scripts/effects.mjs list` shows each id with its family, `quiet` or `focal`, and its
slots. `<kind>` is the page's ground: `light`, `dark` or `colour`; `<site-kind>` is software, gaming or tech.

```bash
# the effect: an effect hero takes --slots hero; a photograph or UI hero puts it in the one [data-visual] frame: --slots band
node <skill>/scripts/effects.mjs pick --page <site-kind> --palette <kind> --slots hero --quiet --seed <S> --history .taste-skill/effects-history.json
# one card group's still grounds, same family (a pattern or dither effect: --family mesh)
node <skill>/scripts/effects.mjs pick --page <site-kind> --palette <kind> --slots card --family <the effect's family> --exclude <the effect>,<NOUI> --quiet --seed <S> --history .taste-skill/effects-history.json
```

`--quiet` leaves out only the focal grounds, not the patterns. When the slot holds UI (a window, a
fragment, a card group), add the patterns and prints to `--exclude`; `<NOUI>` is
`ruled-grounds,grid-pulse,contour-lines,dot-terrain,dotted-globe,ridgeline,halftone-screen,bayer-dither,ascii-shade,line-engraving,duotone-grade`.

- **Quiet** grounds are an even field that holds UI (`grain-gradient`, `painterly-landscape`,
  `gradient-mesh`, `silk-folds`, `fluted-glass`): a soft field behind UI, never a pattern. **Focal**
  grounds have a subject (`orb-sphere`, `spotlight-cone`, `god-rays`, `aurora-curtains`,
  `caustics`): alone in the hero, nothing over them.
- Two ids a page at most outside the moments; each panel its own `data-fx-seed`. No echo of the
  effect in the close, no pattern panel, no focal tile. `dotted-globe` only by name, for global
  reach, as the effect; `duotone-grade` never on a client's photograph. If `pick` says nothing fits
  a slot, drop the slot.
- A visual on `.ground-inverse` takes an id made for that kind (`--palette dark`).
- Retired or renamed ids never appear: `mesh-gradient` is `gradient-mesh`, `iridescent-foil` is
  `fluted-glass`; `riso-print`, `paper-texture` and `liquid-chrome` are gone.

## Deal the moments and the scene

**Moments** (1 or 2, on every kind): dealt with `moments.mjs pick --page <kind>`, the excludes and the hero rule
exactly as `moments.md` (Deal them) says; pass the scene and the effect so the WebGL total stays
within four. Never a moment in the scene's section or beside it.

**Big scene** (0 or 1, the page's effect): one at random from the scenes whose `types` in
`assets/scenes/index.json` hold the page's site-kind and whose `needs` the brief meets (the table in
`scenes.md`), away from the last three:

```bash
node -e "const fs=require('fs'),f='.taste-skill/scenes-history.json';let h=[];try{h=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(f))}catch{}const a=process.argv.slice(1),k=Math.min(3,a.length-1),p=a.filter(i=>!(k?h.slice(-k):[]).includes(i));const id=p[Math.floor(Math.random()*p.length)];fs.mkdirSync('.taste-skill',{recursive:true});fs.writeFileSync(f,JSON.stringify([...h,id]));console.log(id)" <the fitting ids>
```

When the dealt scene's `needs` turn out unmet, deal again without that id; none when no id is
left. A scene is the hero only when its `restH` is 1; the three hero scenes rest in two screens
today, so they go below the dealt hero as a two-screen section (`scenes.md`, Who gets one). Never
a scene with a moment its `avoidMoments` (in `index.json`) lists, or with its twin: pass the scene
as `--scene <id>` to the moments deal, and `pick` leaves out its avoidMoments and twins itself.
Markup and checks: `scenes.md`.

**Its height (rule 3):** `{"hold": 1}` and `--h` = the scene's `restH`, as `scenes.md` (Its
height) says; no page CSS; the scene's section stays one or two screens like every other.

## Where things sit

- **The effect:** the hero (`.frame.frame--hero` holding a `.stage.stage--fade-b`, or the hero's
  layer), or the one `[data-visual]` frame under an h2 (a window up to 1280x540 at 1440, 342x256 at
  390), or the scene's own section. One `[data-visual]` a page. A hero with an effect in a frame is
  a 5/7 or 6/6 split with the visual right, or moves the effect to its own section; an effect as the
  hero's layer (a game's world, a focal ground) keeps the words on its calm part at 4.5:1.
- **Split frame:** `.frame.frame--split` holding a `.stage`; a window `.at-corner.to-edge` at 56/56,
  cut by the right and bottom; a second piece (`cursor`, `notify`) only over a window's lower-right
  edge (`.at-over`), hidden from 1024 to 1279 and on a phone. Text and UI never share a half.
- **Card panels:** `cards.md` (the panel, the fragment on it, fades, the lit palettes, the loop).
- **Text over an effect** only on its quiet part at 4.5:1 or more; a noise or fog ground never holds
  content.
- **Video** (tech, hero or `[data-visual]` only, as the effect or loop): muted, inline, poster
  first, a 6 to 12 s loop or a story that plays once and holds its last frame, a pause button,
  separate phone and desktop files. On other a still that opens the film on a click.
- **The lit ground** (`<html data-ground>`, tech): system.js gives it to every ground that holds UI,
  so page, card, panel and UI are never four near-black layers.

## Motion and cost

- The effect reacts to the pointer or to time (the scene and a moment may react to scroll); after
  assembling it holds, with no constant churn; ambient cycles 4 s or longer, a drift of a few px a
  second, 2 to 10% of pixels changing in 0.9 s; it is still at rest or has a pause button; it shows
  a poster first and a still fallback under reduced motion, on a phone and when WebGL fails. Never
  sound on entry; pointer play off on touch.
- Draw an effect 20 to 25px larger than its box and clip it. One sample per CSS px or less (0.75
  when large), about 1.5 megapixels, pixel ratio 1.5 at most; noise, particles and ray marching at
  half resolution and 30fps or less. A noise ground is one baked texture drifting on time; a caustic
  net is its flat floor net only.
- Blend modes only for a job inside the effect (a glint), never on text. No glass or frosted look on
  any kind: a menu curtain is a flat 40% dim.
- system.js mounts grounds (`ui.grounds`), never `fx.mountAll` from a page script. After any shader
  change run `lint-glsl.mjs` in `assets/objects/_print-core` and `_scenes`: never a GLSL ES reserved
  word (`flat`, `smooth`, `sample`, `filter`, `input`, `output`...) as a name; every WebGL piece
  shows its still fallback when its shader fails. Speed: `perf.md`.

## Never

- An effect, print, grain, gradient or WebGL on a page of kind other; an effect where a photograph
  belongs.
- A print, dither, grade or filter over a photograph, on any kind.
- A live effect or a moving canvas inside a card; a card that animates on scroll.
- A caption explaining a visual (credits go in the one footer line); blinking or random effects;
  violet or lavender.
- A site's code, assets or signature device copied: take only the generic idea, built from the
  skill's own scenes and moments with the client's content.

# The finish gate

A build is not finished while the checker still finds a FAIL it could fix. `scripts/gate.mjs` runs the
checks that matter, lists what is open, and counts rounds, so a build iterates for real and still ends.

## Arm it

At step 1, before any page exists:

```bash
node <skill>/scripts/gate.mjs --start index.html --kind <kind> --category "<what is sold>" --primary "<main action>"
```

- A framework build names what a browser can open: its dev server's URL (`--start http://localhost:5173/`,
  with the server running when the gate runs) or its built page (`--start dist/index.html --root dist`).
  A built page is checked as built: rebuild before every gate run, or the round is spent on the old build.
  The gate opens only a local page: a file, or a URL on `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, `*.localhost`
  or `*.test`.
- `--start` on a build whose rounds are still open does not reset them: it only updates the page, URL,
  root, kind, category and primary it checks. `--start --new` begins a new build. `--rounds N` (3 by
  default) is set only when a build begins.
- `start.mjs deal` arms the folder as well when no build is open there; `css` and `brand` never do.

## What it does

- **A build is active** while `.taste-skill/build.json` exists in the project folder (or one or two
  folders below), or while `.taste-skill/gate.json` says its rounds are still open: deleting the marker
  does not end a build. A `start.mjs deal` in a folder one or two below an open build joins that build
  instead of arming a second one.
- **The page:** the one named, else the marker's page or URL, else `index.html`, else the only `.html`
  file, else the `index.html` of the only folder below that has one.
- **The checks**, one at a time, each in its own headless Chrome with a fresh profile:
  `consistency.mjs --quick --widths 1440,390` (with the kind the page declares, else the marker's, and its category, primary and
  root, as step 6 runs it) and `assets/layout/check.mjs --sizes 1440x900,390x844`. The consistency run includes
  `empty-area` (a section over 35% empty inside its container WARNs, over 50% FAILs) and the `basics`
  block (names, alt, labels, heading order, the Tab walk, lang, head tags, map links, assumed facts):
  their FAILs block like the others; their WARNs (skip-link, share-meta, action-repeat at two,
  assumed, the form's `.example` stand-in) never do. The quick run leaves out what only step 6's full
  run checks: `forms`, `reduced-motion`, `hover-move`, `hover-spill`, `loop-pause`, `hidden-visual`, the scroll walks. The 390 width brings the phone checks (`collide`,
  `tap-size`) and a walk at 320 for anything past the screen (`off-viewport`); `hidden-content` also
  loads the page with scripts off. Plus two read from the files:
  - **kit-edited**: a file the page loads from `assets/` differs from the skill's copy (whitespace,
    quotes, semicolons and commas aside, so a formatter is not an edit). A kit copy from an older skill version
    counts too: copy the current one.
  - **checker-gaming**: the page's own code tests for `navigator.webdriver`, `window.__playwright`,
    `callPhantom` or the checker's `__cc` hooks (code only: a code sample in a string is not a test).
  - **gaming-suspect** (waivable): a user-agent test for "headless", or `aria-hidden` stripped from every
    picture a selector finds. The kit's own `assets/motion/motion.js` tests for `HeadlessChrome` (its
    `shot()`: in a headless browser the counts and the hero entrance stand as written, at their end,
    unless the page sets `data-motion="live"`). An unchanged kit copy is skipped by its text; a build that bundles or ports it
    (a framework's `src/lib/motion.js`, a `dist/assets/index-*.js`) gets this finding for the kit's
    line: waive it with "the kit's motion.js shot() test, ported unchanged" as the reason.
  - **the copy** (waivable): `scripts/copy-lint.mjs --json --kind <kind>` on the page's file, or, when
    the file holds no sections (a built app, a dev server), on the page as the checker's browser built
    it; with neither the copy is listed as not checked, never passed. Its FAILs block (`copy-residue`,
    `copy-slop-word`, `copy-stock-phrase`, a device used twice its budget plus one times or more (two-fragment and number-pair headings, contrast
    frames, negation runs, virtue words; riders, puffery, reveals and repeated promises only WARN), a
    brand coined as Kestrel or Halcyon); its WARNs are listed and never block (`copy.md`,
    `copy-tells.md`; `copy-brand-word` is a listed word inside the client's own name). These are
    copy-lint's ids; the checker's copy-headline, copy-fact and the rest are its own. No browser: under
    a second.

  A file whose text is a kit file's is the kit's, wherever it sits. The two checkers' ids for one fault of
  one section (section-height / screen-height / screen-short, one-section / neighbour) are one finding.
  A full run takes a few minutes on a CPU Chrome.
- **WARNs never block,** but for two house rules the checker only WARNs and the gate holds as FAILs:
  `hero-enter` (the hero has no `data-enter`, or the head line that sets `html.m-enter` is missing) and
  `moment-none` (the page deals no moment). The first few WARNs are listed.
- **Waivers.** A FAIL you judge false goes in `.taste-skill/waivers.json`:

  ```json
  [{ "check": "one-section", "target": "section#visit", "reason": "the hours list is one screen at 390; the check counts the phone bar" }]
  ```

  `check` is the finding's id, `target` a part of where it is (3+ characters, or the whole of a short
  where), `reason` 12+ characters.
  One waiver covers one finding: a target that matches several is ignored and says "name one". Each
  copy word, stock phrase or residue hit is its own finding, named by the word and its sentence; a copy
  device used as a tic is one finding, waived only by its whole where as the gate prints it (its count
  and hits), so nothing added later is covered. A word the client's own copy uses (the brief quotes it)
  is waived hit by hit with the brief as the reason. A waived
  FAIL is printed as WAIVED: it goes in the report. kit-edited and checker-gaming cannot be waived. More
  than 5 waivers is itself a FAIL: "too many waivers: fix instead".
- **Rounds** (`.taste-skill/gate.json`). A run whose page or waivers changed since the last round is a
  round; a manual rerun of an unchanged page is not. A hook stop before the gate's first run by hand in
  the build is no round either: it lists the FAILs and blocks (its blocks are counted apart), and the
  first run by hand counts that page's round, so a question to the user mid-build costs nothing. After
  a hook block, the next finish on the unchanged page is allowed once without a round (a question to
  the user: the block says "just stop again"); other finishes on it block twice without a round
  ("nothing changed"), then each counts as one; a change starts that count again. Below the last
  round: FAIL, fix, finish again. At the last round the gate says once "rounds used up": stop fixing,
  put the open FAILs in the report, finish. Every later finish is allowed. A PASS, and the last
  round's OPEN, rename `build.json` to `build.done.json`, so a later deal starts a build of its own.
- **When the user ends it.** Only when the user tells you to stop, or to ship the page as it is:
  `gate.mjs --done "<what they said>"` (12+ characters) closes the build with their words: status
  `done` in `gate.json`, `build.json` renamed to `build.done.json`, every later finish allowed. Its
  last line is `GATE: DONE (...)`; put it, their words and the open FAILs in the report. Never for
  your own call that the page is good enough: that is what the rounds are for.
- **It never traps an agent.** Every block is counted in `.taste-skill/gate-blocks.json`, which `--start`
  never clears; past the rounds plus 4 blocks for one build (the blocks before the first run by hand
  have that many of their own), or 30 in 6 hours in the folder, every finish is allowed. No page, a framework shell, or checks that crashed or ran past 9.5 minutes block once with
  what to do, then allow. A crashed or timed-out run is stored for its page: a later finish on the
  unchanged page reuses it instead of running the checks again (once more at most, when the agent was
  not yet told). Each check runs with a watchdog that kills it, and its Chrome, if the gate is
  killed; nothing else is ever killed.

## The manual gate

```bash
node <skill>/scripts/gate.mjs index.html
```

Its last line is exactly one of:

```
GATE: PASS
GATE: FAIL <n> (round <k> of <max>)
GATE: OPEN <n> (rounds used up)
GATE: QUICK <n> (not a round; run without --quick to finish)
GATE: SETUP (...)
GATE: ERROR (...)
GATE: OFF (no build active)
GATE: DONE (<the user's words>)      after --done
```

PASS: finish. FAIL: fix what it lists and run it again. OPEN: stop fixing; the open FAILs and the waivers
go in the report. QUICK: a look between rounds, never the last line of a build. SETUP (no page yet, a
framework's source shell, a page that is not local): arm what a browser can open (`--start`, above) and
run it again. ERROR (the checks themselves could not run) or OFF (no build armed here): put the line in
the report and finish; do not rerun. Above the line: every open FAIL with where it is and the fix, every
waiver, the first WARNs. `--quick` (the checker at 1440 and 390, the layout check at 1440) is never a round. The crops are in
`.taste-skill/gate/consistency`.

## As a hook

In Claude Code the skill's own frontmatter adds the gate as a Stop hook once the skill is invoked. The
command is one POSIX `sh` line (Git Bash on Windows, `sh` on macOS and Linux) that runs the first
`gate.mjs` it finds, in this order: `$CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR/scripts/`, `$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/scripts/` and
`$CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/skills/taste-skill/scripts/` (a plugin install), each only when the variable is
set; then the install folders by name, `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/skills/design-taste-frontend/`,
`$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.agents/skills/design-taste-frontend/`, `~/.claude/skills/design-taste-frontend/`
and `~/.agents/skills/design-taste-frontend/` (`npx skills`, `install.sh`). When it finds none, the stop
is allowed with no hook error; when the folder has a `.taste-skill` it writes
`.taste-skill/gate-hook-missing.txt` (the time and the variables it read), and when a build is armed
there or one folder below it prints `tasteskill gate: gate.mjs not found (CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=...)` on
stderr, so a hook that never reached the gate shows in the transcript. A skill installed under another
folder name, other apps, or a Claude Code without skill hooks take one of these. Each runs in every
session of the project and finds a build in its folder or one or two below. Where none is active it
exits at once, but once for a tasteskill page (a `page-type` meta) changed in the last day in the
folder or one below that was never armed: it says how to arm it (`.taste-skill/unarmed.json` records
that it told). It holds only the first session it blocks, lets an orchestrator
whose builds sit in two or more folders below stop, and ignores a build idle for 24 hours. Replace
`/path/to/skill` with the skill's folder.

**Claude Code**, `.claude/settings.json` (blocks with JSON on stdout):

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "Stop": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "node \"/path/to/skill/scripts/gate.mjs\" --hook claude", "timeout": 600 } ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Codex**, `.codex/hooks.json` (the same output as Claude Code: `{"decision":"block","reason":...}`):

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "Stop": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "node \"/path/to/skill/scripts/gate.mjs\" --hook codex", "timeout": 600 } ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

**Antigravity**, `.agents/hooks.json` (it answers `{"decision":"continue","reason":...}` to keep the agent working):

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "Stop": [
      { "hooks": [ { "type": "command", "command": "node \"/path/to/skill/scripts/gate.mjs\" --hook antigravity", "timeout": 600 } ] }
    ]
  }
}
```

In every mode the gate allows a stop by printing nothing and exiting 0. It reads the hook's JSON on stdin
(2 seconds at most) for `cwd` and `session_id`; `stop_hook_active` does not end the rounds early, the round
count in `gate.json` does.

Every hook call leaves one entry in `gate.json`'s `history`, an allowed stop too: `"mode": "hook"`, the
`host`, `"decision": "allow"` or `"block"` and a short `reason` (a run of the checks adds its status, FAIL
count and round). After a PASS or with the rounds used up it goes in that build's `gate.json`; with no
build armed, in the newest `gate.json` in the folder or one or two below, else in the folder's own
`.taste-skill` when there is one. It never makes a new `.taste-skill` folder, and never writes into a build
below that an orchestrating session does not hold. An entry alone keeps the file's time, so it never
makes an idle build look active.

A hook added by a skill belongs to the main session: a subagent that loads the skill is not held, and its
parent is held instead. Run the manual gate inside a subagent.

# Icons

A page that names a tool shows that tool's real logo, in its own colours. A file card that says Google Docs
carries the Google Docs icon, a Word file the Word file icon. Never draw a look-alike, never put a letter in a
circle or a generic page glyph where a real icon exists. A fictional client's own mark is designed, never borrowed.

`scripts/icons.mjs` is the one resolver. Pages, `diagram.js` and every other part read the SVG files it writes;
nothing fetches, tints or judges an icon at runtime, and no page calls a CDN for an icon.

## Where they come from

| set | source (pinned) | holds | drawings licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `logos` | `cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/gilbarbara/logos` at commit `d6960edc1b73` (26 Oct 2026; the repository has no tags) | about 1,500 brands in full colour: the first choice | CC0 (LICENSE.txt at the commit) |
| `si` | `simple-icons` 16.30.0 | one-colour marks painted in the brand hex: the fallback, only where no colour mark exists | CC0 |
| `file` | `@iconify-json/vscode-icons` 1.2.30 | file types in colour (pdf, markdown, zip, Word, Excel, PowerPoint): a document type, never a brand | MIT |
| `ui` | `@iconify-json/lucide` 1.2.100 | interface glyphs, one line set | ISC |

`si` is used for Google Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Chat and Tasks, Calendly, Evernote, QuickBooks, Revolut and the
console and game-store marks (PlayStation, Epic Games, Riot, Battle.net, itch.io, Roblox, EA, Ubisoft, Rockstar, Valve,
CurseForge, Modrinth, GOG). Xbox and Nintendo are in no permitted set: name the console in type, never a drawn
mark; a game's store row is Steam, PlayStation and Epic Games (`apps --tag gaming`). The Google editors are in their brand blue, green and yellow; the Microsoft Office
marks exist in no permitted source, so a Word, Excel or PowerPoint file card uses the file-type icon (`docx`, `xlsx`, `pptx`).

**theSVG (the `brands` set) was dropped.** Its package is MIT, which covers the compilation only; the licence it
records per mark is its own label, not a grant by the owner, and 37 of its Microsoft marks say "no express redistribution
licence supplied". A press-kit download is not a path this skill takes. `brands:` ids now fail with a message that says so.

Every mark is still its owner's trademark: nominative use only. Name tools the product really works with, never imply
endorsement. The footer carries "Product names and logos are trademarks of their owners" and the site carries
`icons-credits.json` (file, set, source with the commit, licence, trademark flag, the brand's site).

## Commands

`node <skill>/scripts/icons.mjs ...` from the site root:

- `find google docs`: what matches, in every set, with licence.
- `apps --tag gaming`: the curated list, 458 apps and 38 file types by short name (`google-docs`, `steam`, `pdf`);
  `list --tags` shows the tags (dev, ai, gaming, engine, hardware, chips, cloud, db, monitoring, payments, social ...).
  Interface glyphs: `list --set ui --tag gaming` (435: gamepad-2, swords, microchip, circuit-board ...).
- `fetch google-docs slack file:pdf2 ui:arrow-right --out assets/icons`: writes the files, prints the tags to paste.
- `scan index.html --out assets/icons`: fetches every icon a page names (diagram specs, `data-diagram` preset names, `data-icon`).
  Run it last, so a finished page has no missing icon.
- `check`: does every entry resolve; lists wordmarks, one-colour fallbacks, black and violet marks.
- `measure`: maintenance. Measures every colour mark's drawn box in headless Chrome (CPU flags, closed by its own PID) into
  `index.json` `boxes`; `fetch` crops to it. Run it when the curated list changes (`--profile <dir>` sets the Chrome profile).
- From code: `import { resolveIcon } from './icons.mjs'`.

Each written file carries the decision: `data-ic="violet"`, `"ink"` or `"paper"` on the root, so `diagram.js` and any page treat it
as `icons.mjs` printed it.

## Which one

- Brand or file type: the colour icon, from the curated list first (`logos`), a `si` mark only where the list says so.
- Interface glyphs (search, arrow, check, a feature point): `ui:` only, never a second line set. A glyph is an inline svg and takes the text colour.
- One-colour (`--mono`) is better in a row of customer logos, in footer social links, and where a brand has no colour version.
  A multi-tone mark keeps its detail in one colour: its paper-coloured parts are cut out of the silhouette instead of filling solid.
- Black marks (GitHub, Apple, X) carry `ic-ink`: icon.css turns them white on a dark ground. A wordmark-only logo (Stripe, NVIDIA, Go)
  carries `ic-wide`: print it with `--tile`, which gives it a wide tile.
- Light marks that vanish on a light tile are not in the list (Wise, Klarna were dropped for it).

### The violet rule (a judgement, stated)

"Never violet or lavender" is a rule for the page's own design. A third-party logo is its owner's mark and is not
recoloured, but a block of violet breaks the palette. By the share of coloured fills that are violet (`check` prints it; deep navy is not violet):

- Half or more (Stripe, Twitch, Google Forms, Terraform, Datadog, ClickUp, Loom, Kotlin, C#, .NET, Bootstrap, ESLint ...): flagged
  `[violet]`. A tool the product really works with keeps its own colours: `fetch` or `scan` it with `--colour` (without it the mark
  prints in the text colour, and a grey stand-in of a known logo is a fault). The violet ban covers the page's
  palette, never a third-party logo; `--mono` only for a row of customer logos.
- Under half (Figma 20%, Google Drive 14%): printed as drawn; the real logo is what makes the page look official. `--mono` prints it in one colour.

## How they sit

Link `assets/icons/icon.css` after system.css. `.ic-tile` is the soft tile behind a logo (a light tile on a dark
ground, so every colour reads); `.ic-row` a list row; `.ic-chip` a name with an icon; `.ic-stack` overlapping
tiles; `.ic-grid--mosaic` with `.ic-cell` an integration grid; `.ic-file` and `.ic-file--tile` a file card;
`.ic-point` a glyph with a short text. Sizes 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, 40, 48, 56. Nothing animates. `assets/icons/demo.html`
shows the mosaic, the file cards, all 458 tools by kind, a dark page and the glyphs (every icon sits in `assets/icons/demo/`).

Shapes: `fetch` crops a mark to its measured drawing (2% margin) and gives it a shape class from the cropped proportions:
`ic-wide` (over 1.8:1), `ic-land` (over 1.25:1), `ic-tall` (under 0.8:1: Google Docs, Figma). A tile sizes a landscape mark to 70% of its
width and a portrait one to 68% of its height. The `file` set is not cropped on purpose.

File cards, integration grids and "reads from" lists use real icons at 20 to 40px, never a grey box. A logo keeps its own
proportions and colours.

# Moments

A moment is the award-site part of a page (house rule 8): the one place, or two, where a page does
something a visitor remembers, in a section of its own; besides it the page has only the hero's
entrance and the hover layer (`motion.md`, The rule). Each is a folder in `assets/moments/<id>/`
(`moment.js`, `moment.css`, `meta.json`, a full `demo.html`); `index.json` lists them,
`gallery.html` links the demos and `moments.js` runs them. Eighteen folders: five retired
(`headline-arrives`, `closing-lift`, `lines-rise`, `window-parallax`, `word-rotate`), and thirteen
dealt by kind (below).

**Which pages: every page.** One moment on a short page, two on a long one (eight sections or more,
in two different sections), never three, on every kind. The place's short page (under 8
photographs, `sections.md` section 4) skips the type moment: its one moment is `picture-develops`
on the section's photograph (`--fits section --photo`, dealt again with `--exclude photo-chapters`
when it gives `photo-chapters`), or, with no photograph, `word-highlight` in a one-screen statement
section of its own, so the page is four screens.

| page kind | dealt from | look |
|---|---|---|
| place (cafe, bakery, guesthouse, shop, gym; a studio with a door is passed as `--page place`, since `--page studio` reads as service) | `photo-chapters`, `picture-develops` (film), `word-highlight` | photographs and type |
| product (site-kind other) | `photo-chapters`, `pinned-chapters`, `picture-develops` (film), `word-highlight` | photographs and type |
| service (firm, clinic, agency, trade) | `photo-chapters`, `pinned-chapters`, `picture-develops` (film), `word-highlight` | photographs and type |
| software, gaming, tech | the eleven that list them: every dealt moment but `photo-chapters` and `picture-develops` | as before 2.5.1 |

Why these for the other kinds: each is led by the client's own photographs or words, moves only in
its own section, costs no WebGL and reads as calm (a hotel, a law firm, a wedding photographer). Not
on them: anything with a shader, WebGL or a liquid or pointer effect (`liquid-hover`,
`liquid-type`, `cursor-spotlight`), anything that reads as a graphic trick (`iris-opens`,
`line-carries-colour`, `letters-assemble`, the halftone of `picture-develops`, and
`giant-type-pass`: a photograph inside letters reads as a template trick, muddies a warm palette
and is a parallax), a loop (`marquee-row`) and a count (`counter-rolls`). On those
pages the two of a long page are the statement moment (`word-highlight`) and one section moment
(the photographs), or the photograph that develops beside one of the chapters moments (two kinds:
one runs once as it enters, the other follows the scroll). `photo-chapters` and `pinned-chapters` never share a page and do different
jobs: photo-chapters tells a story in full-width photographs with one chapter at a time on a panel;
pinned-chapters walks through steps listed beside one frame (how a booking or an order goes).
A moment counts against a tech page's big scene (`effects-usage.md`) as one of its beats.

## Deal them, never choose by taste

```bash
# a place, product or service page: one on a short page, two on eight sections or more
node <skill>/scripts/moments.mjs pick --page place|product|service --count 1|2 --fits section,statement \
  --photo --history .taste-skill/history.json
# a software, gaming or tech page (less a hero moment)
node <skill>/scripts/moments.mjs pick --page <kind> --count 1|2 --fits section,statement \
  [--scene <id>] [--effects <ids>] [--contexts <n>] [--photo] --history .taste-skill/history.json
# a hero moment on tech (0 or 1): the same with --count 1 --fits hero; kept only when the dealt hero lists it
```

- **`--page`** is the page's kind (`SKILL.md` section 1: `software`, `gaming`, `tech`, `place`,
  `product` or `service`; `ai`, `saas`, `technical-product`, `cafe`, `bakery`, `guesthouse`,
  `hotel`, `shop`, `studio`, `agency`, `firm`, `clinic` and a few more are read too). A word that
  names no kind (`other` is three kinds) stops the deal with exit 1: say which.
- **`--photo`** on every place, product or service page (they all have photographs): without it
  the photo moments drop out and a long page cannot be dealt two.
- **`--fits section,statement`:** a statement is a section of its own, so the letters, liquid type,
  word-highlight and the counter come only with it; `section` alone deals none of them.
- **No kind needs `--exclude`:** each pool is what lists the kind in `meta.json` (the short page's
  `photo-chapters`, above, is the one case).
  `picture-develops` is dealt only in its film look, on place, product and service; its halftone
  look stays in the kit as `data-moment-opts='{"look": "print"}'` with its print-shop demo, never
  dealt. A dealt scene's twins and avoidMoments are left out by `--scene <id>` itself.
- **The hero moment** (0 or 1, never on a big-scene hero) is kept only when the dealt hero lists it
  in `heroes.json` (`moments[].id`): that is `liquid-hover` on `split` and
  `photo`, `cursor-spotlight` on `product`, `collage`, `film` and `centred`, `liquid-type` on
  `statement` (tech, a headline of six words or fewer), and none on the others. Off touch only;
  reduced motion rests. Two moments in all at most.
- **The WebGL budget.** A page holds at most 4 live contexts (`perf.md`). The deal adds up what the
  page already spends and never deals a moment whose own `webgl` (in its `meta.json`: only
  `liquid-hover` has 1) would push the total over 4: pass the big scene as `--scene <id>` (its `webgl`
  is read from `assets/scenes/index.json`), each dealt effect in `--effects a,b` (counted as one
  each, the worst case) and anything else in `--contexts <n>` (an object, a component with a canvas).
  The deal prints the total it reached.
- **The rest of the deal.** Placed in different sections. The history's `moments` list is read as
  cycles: once every moment that fits has been dealt, the next cycle starts empty, so an id comes
  back only after all the others and never straight after itself (the three dealt last stay out
  even across a cycle's end). Never two of one kind (hover and liquid count as one: one pointer
  effect a page), never two of one slot, never two that avoid each other, a moment that needs a
  photograph only with `--photo`; on a place, product or service page one statement and one
  section, or two kinds (`picture-develops` with a chapters moment). Write each id, its section and its purpose in the plan (`motion.md`, Why it moves). A dealt moment with
  nothing to carry is dealt again with it added to `--exclude`.
- **Retired** (`meta.retired`, weight 0, never dealt): `headline-arrives` (every hero now enters
  through the motion layer, `motion.md`, The hero's entrance; a moment that also moves the headline
  would be a second entrance) and `closing-lift` (it needs a closing band of its own and its words stand on a
  gradient over the photograph); since 2.5.1 also `lines-rise` (every hero's lines already rise on
  load), `window-parallax` (a parallax on a photograph) and `word-rotate` (the `word` hero carries
  its own live word, `layout-v4.md`). `magnetic-button` (CK-94) is gone.

## The still rule (every moment, no exception)

Every moment has a static variant for a **phone** and for **reduced motion**, and a finished state
without script or when its module fails. The loader decides: it hands each moment a `lib` whose
`reduced()` answers `lib.still()`, which is true under `prefers-reduced-motion` and on a phone (under
640px wide, or a touch screen turned sideways under 500px tall). A moment written against `reduced()`
therefore shows its finished state there, and the host carries `data-moment-still="reduced"`,
`"phone"` or `"card"`. **Phones still get a moment:** the ones light enough for a phone (one
picture or one paragraph at a time; transform, clip, filter or colour) say `export const phone =
true` in their `moment.js` and `"phoneRuns": true` in `meta.json`, and run there; only reduced
motion and a card keep them still. Those are `word-highlight`, `picture-develops` (film) and
`photo-chapters` (from 600px of height), which covers every place, product and service deal. The answer is taken when the moment mounts (a window resized across 640px
applies it on the next load; `pinned-chapters` and `photo-chapters` ask again on resize). Each `meta.json` says what the
still shows (`reduced`, `phone`). Hover moments do nothing on touch screens either.

**Nothing on a card moves on scroll** (house rule). A moment sits on a hero, a statement, one
section, a transition or the close, never in a card, a plan, a result or a bento cell: the loader
leaves one that does still (`data-moment-still="card"`, `data-moments-card` on `<html>`) and
`moments.mjs check` calls it a fault.

## Put one on the page

The host is a section of the page (or, for the text moments, the headline or the row inside it);
mark it as the moment's header comment shows (`data-moment="<id>"`, options in `data-moment-opts`).
Every section stays one or two screens tall (`layout-v4.md`, `--h`), live and at rest, but the two
chapters moments: `photo-chapters` is (hold + 1) screens live (three for three chapters, four for
four or five; write no `--h` and no `data-screen` on it: the checker and the layout check both read a
live photo-chapters section as whole screens, four at most) and both are as tall as their content at rest. A transition's
host is the whole section that sits on the new ground, a statement moment is one section with its h2
first, a marquee or counter row merges into the section above as its last row. In `<head>`, the one line plus a `modulepreload` for
the loader, its lib and the dealt moment:

```html
<script>document.documentElement.classList.add('mo-js');setTimeout(()=>document.documentElement.classList.add('mo-safe'),2500)</script>
<link rel="modulepreload" href="assets/moments/moments.js"><link rel="modulepreload" href="assets/moments/lib.js"><link rel="modulepreload" href="assets/moments/<id>/moment.js">
```

Then the loader once. On a page with `system.js`, `system.js` imports it and waits for it. On a page
without, the demo pages' tag at the end of `<body>`:

```html
<script type="module" src="assets/moments/moments.js"></script>
```

The loader links each moment's CSS and starts it; `<html data-moments-ready>` says when. A failed
module gets `data-moment-failed` and the class `mo-safe` on its own element, which the moment's CSS
reads as "show the finished state now". A demo's copy and photographs are placeholders. Every moment
takes the page's tokens (`--bg`, `--ink`, `--muted`, `--accent`, `--line`, the display face).

A moment's section in a page is copied from one of the two page models, which mount moments inside
a starter page and pass the checker: `assets/moments/_demo/in-page.html` (a place:
`photo-chapters`, `word-highlight`) and `in-page-service.html` (a service: `pinned-chapters`,
`picture-develops` in its film look). A moment's own `demo.html` shows it alone and is not a page
model.

## Rules

- **The kind's count, an id once.** `data-moments-over` and `data-moments-repeat` on `<html>` are faults.
- **No random effects as you scroll.** A scroll moment is scrubbed to the scrollbar inside its own
  section, which stays one or two screens tall (`photo-chapters` three or four), and does one purposeful thing; at the section's top
  and bottom it shows a finished state (every transition and `letters-assemble` finish before the
  section's top is a fifth of the screen down), so each judge tile shows one whole section. No card,
  row or tile ever enters on scroll. `consistency.mjs` reports a scroll finding inside the dealt
  `[data-moment]` section; that one is expected, any other is a fault.
- **Content is readable without the motion:** the words are in the HTML, in their finished place; a
  moment never hides a headline on load (the hero's own entrance is the motion layer's, `motion.md`).
- **Photo-led on the other kinds:** a place, product or service page's moment carries the client's
  own photographs (or library ones that pass `photos.md`), each used once on the page, and its
  words are the page's real copy; never a stand-in picture to give the moment something to move.
- **One count a page:** `counter-rolls` or `data-m-count` (`motion.md`), never both.
- **Nothing blinks, bounces or overshoots.** Ease-outs (cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1) for a settle),
  600-1,000 ms for a reveal, 1.6-1.8 s for a photograph developing; a scrubbed wipe or change takes
  about half of its chapter's share of the scroll and holds for the rest; a loop runs its rounds and
  rests, or carries a pause button.
- **The page's edges.** A moment's text sits in a `.container` or `.wrap` like every other section: its
  words end on the page's left and right edges. A transition's cover is an inset panel inside the host
  section with an even gutter on every side (card corners, never touching the section's edges), its
  line or ring inside the panel; every heading, paragraph, button and picture appears whole, never cut
  by the line or the disc (each moment's `meta.json`, `look`, says how).
- **Cost:** no WebGL but `liquid-hover` (tech only) (one context, only near the screen; a plain photograph without
  WebGL or when the shader fails). `liquid-type` is one SVG filter on one headline, on only while a
  ripple is alive. Every other moment costs CSS variables, a transform or a clip and a passive
  listener.
- **One pointer effect a page:** a hover or liquid moment rules out `fx-button`, `fx-spotlight` and an
  object that turns to the pointer, and the reverse; `pick` never deals two of them.
- **Photographs:** `giant-type-pass` and `liquid-hover` (tech) want mid to dark tones with edges and detail; a
  pale dusk sky reads lavender in a letter and a flat sea shows no ripple. Never violet or lavender.
- **No captions;** the photograph's credit goes in the footer line.

## Check it

- `node <skill>/scripts/moments.mjs check <page.html> --page <kind> [--scene <id>] [--effects a,b] [--contexts n]`
  reads the built page: how many moments, any twice, retired, off its page kind (a WebGL or effect
  moment on a place is off its kind), in a card, holding a figcaption, two that avoid each other, two
  of one slot on a place, product or service page, the WebGL total against 4, a missing loader. Exit 1
  on a fault.
- `node <skill>/scripts/moments.mjs shoot --out shots/moments --profile <own chrome dir> --port 5720 --only <id> [--reduced]`
  shoots the demo's start, middle and end states at 1440 and 390 in the skill's headless Chrome (WebGL
  on the CPU); the end must be the finished section. Under `--reduced`, and at 390 for a moment
  without `phoneRuns`, it also checks the still rule: the host must say `data-moment-still` and no
  animation may run inside it (a line `STILL?` otherwise). `--probe "<js expression>"` prints a value after each state.
- The headless Chrome draws WebGL on the CPU, so `liquid-hover` shows a fainter ripple there than on a
  GPU and its end state waits 6 s to be the plain picture; a text or scroll moment looks the same on both.

A missing or invisible hover layer is a fault on every kind (round C: a fintech, a cafe and a guesthouse page lost motion points because a hovered card or button showed no change), and since 2.5.1 so is a page without its hero entrance or its dealt moment. This file holds every hover, press, loop and reduced-motion number; other files point here. ## The rule: every page moves, in three places Every page, every kind, has the same three layers of motion, and nothing else moves: 1. **The hero's entrance** on load, once (below): the h1 line by line, then its lead and buttons, the picture settling. About 1.1 s, then the hero stands. 2. **One dealt moment** in a section of its own (two on a long page: eight sections or more), big enough to remember: `moments.mjs pick --page ` deals it (`moments.md`). On a place, product or service page it is photo- or type-led (photographs that change in place, a photograph that develops, a statement that lights up); shader and WebGL effects stay on tech, gaming and software (house rule 8: a cafe, bakery, guesthouse or shop gets photographs, never a shader). 3. **The hover and press layer** below, on every link, button, linked card and linked photograph, and the swaps a click or a tap makes (a tab on software, a peek-list's photograph). On tech, gaming and software pages also: loops inside a card's visual (diagram pulses included), one timed loop in the hero or the `[data-visual]` frame, one count, and the effect and scene `effects-usage.md` deals. The card, its panel and the window never move: no zoom, tilt or camera pan inside the window. - One subject per cycle (a pointer clicks, a status turns, a bar fills, a line is written): one change every 1 to 2 s, each change 300ms or less. Several subjects: the next one each cycle. A changing label never shows two words at once. - One fragment loop per card group (`data-ui-loop`); the other fragments hold their finished picture and play while the pointer rests on their card. A small diagram card's pulse is that card's own loop, on the same cycle, restart and pause rules (house rule: pulses running along the lines); system.js never holds it (`data-ui-still` does not reach a diagram). Below the hero, two loops are never on one screen: in a group with a pulsing diagram, give the fragments `data-ui-still` too, or hold the diagram with `data-dg-still` (it then plays under the pointer). - A page's own CSS loop sits in `[data-m-loop]`, every keyframe on `var(--m-cycle)`, `--m-still` (0 to 1) the finished frame, a 48px band (`--m-safe`) kept clear for the pause button. - Life signs inside the looping visual only: spinner 1s (12 to 16px, then a check), live dot 2.4s (the dot still, a ring grows and fades), caret 1s with a hard step inside a field, level bars .6s. No typing dots, no lone pulsing dot elsewhere, no block cursor after a headline. - Kinds of card story (each in a box of fixed height): a prompt types at 12 to 20 characters a second and holds; an answer streams about a bubble a second; a notification enters at the top and the oldest leaves through the fade; a checklist ticks about once a second; a calendar's events fade in one by one; a pointer glides about 200px in 1 s, presses (scale .96 at least, a 28px ring) and holds. A speaker or avatar front item changes no more than every 3 s. A chart stays still. - Not yet placed, so not used: a stepping slot strip, a before/after divider, path-following items, a dock tab that grows, a pointer-linked mascot, a comet along a hero strand. ## Tech budget - **One timed loop** a page, in the hero or the `[data-visual]` frame, in whatever form (a story, a reel, a lit border, a live ground, a turning object, a marquee); its life signs are part of it. One timed loop plus the one effect at most; with a live effect in the hero, no other timed loop runs. Never two self-moving things in one 900px window, never two loops in one panel. Card loops (one per card group), diagram pulses (one per diagram card) and the dealt moments are outside this count. - **A count** once a page (`data-m-count` or the `counter-rolls` moment, never both): on load in the hero (1000ms, 1.2 s at most), or as the dealt counter moment in its own section. On the open ground, never in a card, panel or `[data-visual]`; its width reserved; the final figure in the HTML, shown under reduced motion, without script and on phones; never a year, price or phone number. A live counter changes only its last one to three digits. - **Load:** the hero's entrance above, on every kind. On tech also at most one load-once motion inside the `[data-visual]` frame (a visual assembling, 600 to 1200ms), settled by 1.5 s; a click swap 400 to 600ms. No gate, loader or intro. - **Pause:** anything still moving 5 s after it is seen has one round pause button per panel: a solid 32px disc, 12px in from the bottom-right (in a card beside its title), always shown or fading in on hover and focus, the same size and place on every card, never over copy, never on a still. A click freezes the frame and swaps to a play glyph (`ui.pausable(panel, ctrl)` for your own movers). Scroll-driven moments need none. - **Timed loops start on load** and never start, stop or resume on scroll; an IntersectionObserver only mounts lazily. A canvas may skip drawing off screen only on a clock from load, so no visible start shows on return. A hidden tab may pause everything. ## Scroll - **Outside the dealt moment's section (and the tech page's big scene), on every kind:** nothing animates on scroll. No card, row or tile reveal of any kind (fade, rise, stagger, mask wipe), no parallax or drift, no scroll-snap, scroll-tinted ground, progress line, scroll-spy marker or count on view. - **Every kind:** the one or two dealt moments may follow the scroll, each inside its own section (`data-moment`; on tech also the big scene, `data-big-scene` with `{"hold": 1}`), which stays 1H or 2H (`scenes.md`, Its height; `photo-chapters` is 3H or 4H live, about two thirds of a screen a chapter, `moments.md`), pinned only with `position: sticky` inside that box. A scroll moment is scrubbed to the scrollbar (it runs back on the way up) and shows a finished state at both ends; an enter moment (`picture-develops`) runs once, 1.6 to 1.8 s. Its text is live and visible without the motion (opacity 1, 4.5:1 at every step); reduced motion and no script show the finished still; phones run the light ones (`word-highlight`, the film develop, `photo-chapters`: transform, clip, filter or colour, no WebGL) and get the still of the rest; `perf.mjs` passes. It never moves a card, a photograph, pricing, an FAQ, a quote block or the footer. Driven by native `animation-timeline`, a passive scroll read written to a custom property once a frame, or GSAP ScrollTrigger scoped to that section without its pin (tech only). No smooth-scroll library (Lenis, Locomotive, ScrollSmoother) on any page, no animation library at all on other: the kit's moments need none. - The header and the phone bar look the same at every scroll position; the bar only comes up once the hero's button has scrolled away and steps down while the screen shows one of its actions (system.js, 240ms, at once under reduced motion). ## Reduced motion, no script, phones Colours still change; menus fade; a press shows as a deeper tone instead of a move; the tab indicator and the switch knob jump to their place; the tick appears at full size; the underline appears without travelling (`motion.css`, reduced motion: `transition-property` limited to opacity and colours on links, `.m-tab-ind`, `.m-switch::before`, `.m-check::before`). The hero stands as written. Every loop, effect, moment and scene shows its finished frame, marquees stand as a still row, numbers show their final text, pause buttons are hidden. On a phone card loops and effects hold their finished picture or poster, heavy canvases become stills, there are no hover states and no pointer simulations; the hero still enters, and the moments light enough for a phone run there (`moments.md`, The still rule), so a phone page moves in two places too. ## Never - A card, row or tile that reveals, staggers, slides or fades in as the page scrolls; parallax on text; a scroll scrub outside the dealt moment's section (and the tech page's scene); a shader or WebGL moment on a place, product or service page. - A section heading that rises on every section, a second hero entrance, an entrance longer than about 1.1 s, or an entrance that hides text a visitor could already be reading. - A card that tilts, flips, scales, follows the pointer or glows at the cursor; a magnetic button. - A carousel, a slider that advances by itself, timed tabs, a rotating notice, a logo marquee. - Blinking at random: twinkling dots, glitter, flicker, hue cycling, scrambled text; every change shows a state, a step or real data. - A loop that plays once (outside a card story's replay), a card loop's cycle over 4 s, two loops in one panel. - A hover slower than its token, an overshooting ease, a delay before a button reacts, a focus ring that animates, a second underline or indicator style, an animated width, height or margin.

# Performance budget Run `node scripts/perf.mjs ` (Node 22 or later) on every finished page. It loads the page in headless CPU Chrome at 1440 and 390 wide, waits until the effects near the viewport are mounted, scrolls to the bottom and prints PASS, WARN or FAIL. Fix every FAIL. `--json ` also writes the result to that file; `--runs N` sets the number of timing loads (default 3). Reading the numbers: - **Timing is a median of 3 loads** with the spread printed (`runs 3, 33..161`). One load on a CPU is noise; a wide spread means the host was busy. - **Host load** is sampled before and after. Above 50% the check says so and caps timing at WARN: rerun when the machine is idle before believing a timing FAIL. - **FCP and LCP are CPU-rendered.** Compare pages with each other, never with field data. - **WebGL off is a proxy, not a verdict.** SwiftShader runs shaders on the CPU and would swamp the main thread, so long tasks and blocking time come from loads where every WebGL piece shows its still fallback. That is different work from the shader: shader compile and link on a real GPU is not measured, and the INFO line with WebGL on is for orientation only. - Counts (images, contexts, modules) and bytes are exact; they do not depend on host load. | Check | WARN | FAIL | |---|---|---| | Transfer (text gzipped) | above 1500 KiB | above 3000 KiB | | Images total / largest single image | above 1200 / 350 KiB | above 2400 / 700 KiB | | JS parsed / CSS | above 450 / 120 KiB | above 900 / 250 KiB | | Requests | above 60 | above 110 | | Font families / files / bytes | above 2 / 4 / 160 KiB | above 3 / 6 / 320 KiB | | `` without width and height (or CSS aspect-ratio) | 1 to 3 | 4 or more | | `` below the fold and not lazy | 1 to 3 | 4 or more | | Oversized images, ``, CSS background and SVG (natural over 2.2x the shown width) | 1 to 3 | 4 or more | | Photos as CSS or SVG background below the fold (cannot be lazy) | 1 to 3 | 4 or more | | WebGL contexts live (load, bottom, peak) | | above 4 (hard cap) | | WebGL contexts made over the whole scroll | above 12 | above 24 | | Long tasks / blocking time, median, WebGL off | above 8 / 1.5 s | above 20 / 4 s | | FCP / LCP, median | above 2.5 / 4.5 s | above 4.5 / 8 s | | Layout shift, median | above 0.1 | above 0.25 | | Effect, object or component module loaded, never mounted | 1 or 2 | 3 or more | | Broken request, sideways overflow | | any | Sizes are KiB (1024 bytes). The 2.2x rule already covers a 2x screen; a photo that is also upscaled (natural under 0.75x shown) warns. "Never mounted" counts entry files only (`effect.js`, `object.js`, `component.js`, a ui `fragment.js`); shared helpers such as `photo-kit` never count. An object has no marker, so objects are judged by count: more object modules loaded than canvases or fallback hosts drawn. ## Every visual renders A visual that shows only its ground (a blank canvas, a photograph never loaded, a reveal that never fired, a picture caught half drawn) is a fault at every width (house rule 2): every picture slot has a real `src`, `width` and `height`; `consistency.mjs` `empty-visual` and `gl-fallback` find the rest, system.js outlines a failed visual in red, `shoot.mjs` names pictures still loading. ## Usual fixes - **WebGL cost (tech only; 0 contexts on kind other).** At most 4 live contexts per page (house rule): the one effect or big scene plus a dealt moment's own canvas, each showing a poster first, mounted at load or lazily as its section nears the screen (an IntersectionObserver only mounts, it never starts or stops visible motion: `motion.md`). One sample per CSS px or less (0.75 when large), about 1.5 megapixels, pixel ratio 1.5 at most; noise, particles and ray marching at half resolution and 30fps or less; drop the pixel ratio when frames take over 21 to 24ms. Every WebGL piece keeps its still when its shader fails (`effects-usage.md`). After any shader change, `lint-glsl.mjs` in `assets/objects/_print-core` and `_scenes` must exit 0. - **Draw still grounds once.** A ground that does not move is drawn one frame, kept as a picture, its context released. - **Fonts.** At most four font files (`layout-v4.md` section 5; perf.mjs warns above four): preload the regular and the display weight, `font-display: swap`, request only used weights. - **Size images.** AVIF or WebP through `srcset` at 2x the shown width, never more (a full-bleed hero 2880w at 1440, 780w at 390), the hero under 400 KiB and every other photograph under 250 KiB (the check warns at 350 for one image), the page's images under 2,400 KiB at 1440 (the table's FAIL; 1,200 warns), `width` and `height` (or an `aspect-ratio`) on every one and a `--g-alt` fill while it loads. Lazy and `decoding="async"` below the first screen, never lazy in it; the hero eager with `fetchpriority="high"`. A photo below the fold is an ``, not a CSS background. A place with 8 to 20 photographs stays fast this way. - **No shift (CLS under 0.1).** Reserve space for images, nav and counters. Animate transform and opacity (colours too); `background-position` only on small text spans; never height, padding or layout. Import only modules the page mounts. - **Scripts.** Deferred modules, no scroll listeners (the tech moments read the scroll as `motion.md` says), no layout reads in move handlers. No entry gate or loader; kind other loads no animation library and no WebGL; a real-time 3D model stays near 2 MB compressed with a poster; video ships separate phone and desktop files. - **Ready flag.** A page may set `document.documentElement.dataset.ready = '1'` when its first screen is built; the check then stops waiting for effects to mount.

# Photographs A place (café, bakery, guesthouse, shop, studio) is its photographs: two or three on every screen, the client's own. Software leads with its real interface; a photograph there is a real person or the real product. A game leads with its own art (key art, in-engine shots, the trailer's poster), never library frames; with no art files its name is set large over a stand-in photograph of its setting from a live search (`sections.md`, Gaming), never an effect or a random object in its place; a render of its world only when the brief asks for 3D. A physical product without photographs is shown in photographs too: the client's, else stand-ins (below). A photograph never stands where an effect, a drawing or an empty box would. ## Where pictures come from (PH-01, PH-02, PH-05) 1. **The client's own**, shot for the page or on a phone, each file named in the brief. Every `` carries `data-source` (`client`, `commissioned`, `phone`, `supplier`, `illustration`, `library-057`, `stand-in`) and `data-subject`. 2. **The library** (`scripts/photos.mjs`): Wikimedia Commons and Unsplash frames, vetted one by one. They are stock of another place, so they fill **detail slots only**: hands, tools, materials, a process (an oven, dough, a roasting drum, stems, a hammer on a bar). Never the hero, a room, a shopfront, a product or a person, and never more than **1 in 3 of the page's pictures**. `pick` deals exactly that by default and prints the cap with the deal; the draft path below lifts both limits. `fetch` prints `data-source="library-057"`. Every frame was looked at again at 100% (the subject and the centre of the 2400 file) for softness, grade, readable brands and recognisable people; a frame that failed is out of `photos.json` and off disk, and a frame that is a car, a sign or another business's whole room stays `weak` (kept with its credit and its why, no file on disk) and is never dealt; a rating below 7 is never dealt either (`quality`): a whole meeting room, lounge or breakfast room is the same fault. The thin trades get at most as many frames as they hold: wine 0, bar 0, office 3 (a notebook, stacked books, sheets of card), florist 3, farm 3, shop 3, wellness 3, bakery 4, and a workshop by its craft (smith 4, instrument 1, weaving 0, letterpress 0). The rest of the page is the client's own photographs, the object, the real UI or type. 3. **A live search** (`photos.mjs search`, Live search below): licensed Wikimedia Commons photographs of what the library lacks (a product's kind, a yoga studio, a bike workshop's bench, a hotel's building and rooms, a wedding, a game's setting). Each one is a stand-in, looked at full size and listed in the report; `fetch` prints `data-source="stand-in"`. 4. **Nothing**: the real UI, or type; a product's own render only when the brief asks for 3D (`effects-objects.md`, Product renders). Never a near fit, never mood in place of the subject. With no client photographs, say so plainly in the report: strong pages run on a half-day shoot with a local photographer, then a one-morning phone shoot, then products on one backdrop; the library covers details only. The shot list: shopfront straight on, the room from the door, the counter or bench, three products on one surface, hands at work, one detail, each room of a guesthouse; 1x lens, window light, no flash, no filter, landscape and portrait. **The draft path (a place with no client photographs):** `pick --trade --sections --draft-lead --pictures 12` lifts the 1-in-3 cap. `pick` deals one frame per word, so repeat a word for each row or detail (`bar,bar,coffee,coffee,beans,beans`, `rooms,rooms,rooms,breakfast,breakfast`) until it returns 8 or more: a cafe reaches 8 to 12, a guesthouse 9 detail frames. The page stays a whole place page that leads with photographs (house rule 6), the compact page at 8 to 12 frames. The hero is the lead `pick` returns (a cafe's bar). A place whose trade leads with land (a guesthouse, a lodge, a remote inn) passes the region its brief names as `--place ""` (or the brief itself, `--brief BRIEF.md`, which reads the region from it) and leads with that region's landscape: a place hero always carries a photograph when any frame fits, and the `statement` hero is left for a place the library holds no frame of (`sections.md` section 4). Every frame is listed in the report as a stand-in to replace; nothing on the page says so (no caption, no note). **The count decides, not the trade:** when `pick`, with each word repeated until it says "no new motif left", and a live search (`search --trade `, below) has added what passes the full-size look, still returns under eight frames, the page is the short page (PH-07: 2,700 px at most at 1440; `sections.md` section 4, The short page), whatever the trade: a bakery (4 in the library), florist, wellness, office, pottery or a restaurant are examples. No drawn box, grid or effect takes the place of a photograph. Two exceptions, both for a draft or the short page and both named in the report as stand-ins to replace: - **A hero** (`--draft-lead`): the client has no hero photograph yet. A place hero is still Recipe 3: the frame is the full-bleed top photograph with nothing on it. - **The land around a place** (`--place ""`): a place whose brief names its region (Westfjords, Lofoten, the Lake District, a town) is dealt that region's landscape as its lead, because a remote place is sold by where it stands. `--own-land` adds the land sections (area, road) when the brief says the business is that landscape (a tour, a lodge on its own land). Another region's land, a cafe's street and the sky are never dealt (PH-03, PH-50). ## A product without photographs (PH-04) A maker of a physical thing (a bike, a chair, a lamp, a stroller, a device) with no photographs of its own is dealt **no library frame** and **no mood stock**: no forest for "the ride", no groceries for "what it carries", no other trade dealt to fill the page. `pick --product-without-photos` (or a maker's, brand's or company's word: "backpack brand", "electric scooter") says so and prints the search. **The product is still shown, never hidden, in photographs** (in testing: a cargo bike's page that never showed the bike scored 3 of 10): a picture the brief supplies first (a cut-out, a CAD view, its own render; one it names but does not supply counts as missing), else **stand-ins** from `photos.mjs search ""`: the same kind of thing whole and in use (a cargo bicycle for a cargo bike brand, never a wheel for a bicycle), close-ups of the parts the page names, where it lives; no maker's name, logo or badge readable, no face passed off as a customer, one light and grade across the set. The page is the full product page (`sections.md`, Product), never the short page. Every stand-in is listed in the report with the client's photograph to shoot in its place, and nothing on the page says so. A render (`effects-objects.md`, Product renders) only when the brief asks for 3D or a render. The report lists the shots to take: the product on one plain backdrop, three angles, a detail of each part the page names, the product in use. A shop, workshop or rental for every make is a place (`--trade "bike shop"`): it is dealt parts and a basket load for those sections only, and its workshop bench and whole bikes come from a live search. ## Live search (stand-ins for what the library lacks) `photos.mjs search` asks Wikimedia Commons for photographs (JPEG, 1600 px wide or more; CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA or public domain; files named as paintings, drawings, maps, logos or posters left out; one file of a series) and keeps the results in `.taste-skill/found.json` under `--out`, so `fetch` and `credits` take their ids (`f` and a number) like library ids. With `--trade` and no words it runs the trade's own search words: | Trade | search words | |---|---| | yoga, pilates, spa, wellness | yoga studio, yoga class, pilates studio, sauna interior | | pottery, ceramics | pottery wheel, pottery studio, ceramics workshop | | a studio (art, design, photography) | artist studio, design studio, photography studio | | bike shop or workshop | bicycle workshop, bicycle repair stand, bicycle mechanic, city bicycle, cargo bicycle | | hotel, guesthouse, inn | hotel facade, guesthouse, hotel room, hotel bedroom, inn exterior (the building and the rooms: never the library) | | wedding | wedding ceremony, wedding table, wedding bouquet, wedding reception, wedding rings | | restaurant | restaurant kitchen, restaurant interior, chef plating | | workshop by craft | woodworking workshop, blacksmith forge, workshop tools | | bakery, cafe, florist, salon | the trade's own: bakery bread, bakery counter, baker dough; coffee shop interior, espresso machine; florist shop, flower market; barber shop, hair salon | A product searches its own words (`"cargo bicycle"`, `"desk lamp"`, then `"... detail"` and the place it lives); a game its setting in plain words (`"flooded coastal town"`, `"desert mining town"`, `"city at night in rain"`); anything else the subject plainly, two or three words (long phrases find nothing). `--count`, `--min 1200` for a row picture, `--orientation portrait`. Every result is a **candidate**: open its page and look at the file full size. Keep it only when it shows the subject sharp, in plain colour; no readable name, sign or logo of another business (a hotel's name on its facade, a club's name on its wall: drop it or crop it out); no face shown as the client's staff, guests or customers; no landmark passed off as the client's place; one light and grade with the rest of the page. Write its alt text new (the file's title names someone else's place). It is a **stand-in**: the report lists it with the photograph to shoot in its place; nothing on the page says so; its credit goes in the one footer line like any other. ## Pick and fetch ```bash node /scripts/photos.mjs list # trades: detail frames dealt by default, land, can lead node /scripts/photos.mjs list --places # the place names the library knows, for --place node /scripts/photos.mjs pick --trade bakery --sections oven,dough,bread --pictures 14 \ --history .taste-skill/history.json node /scripts/photos.mjs pick --trade cafe --sections hero,bar,bar,coffee,coffee,beans,beans,hands --draft-lead --pictures 12 \ --history .taste-skill/history.json # no client photographs node /scripts/photos.mjs pick --trade guesthouse --sections hero,rooms,rooms --pictures 12 \ --draft-lead --own-land --place "Lofoten, Norway" --history .taste-skill/history.json # a draft only node /scripts/photos.mjs search --trade "yoga studio" --out . # what the library lacks: stand-ins node /scripts/photos.mjs search "cargo bicycle" --count 8 --out . # a product without photographs node /scripts/photos.mjs fetch [--hero ] --out . [--big id] [--lqip] # run from the project root node /scripts/photos.mjs credits --out . --write # the footer line and credits.html; --text for a report ``` - **Order and places.** `pick` prints its follow-up `fetch` with the script's absolute path (forward slashes, quoted when it holds a space) and `--out .`, so it runs as printed from the site folder (from elsewhere, give `--out` the site's path). `fetch` writes the files into `assets/img/` under `--out` (the project's own folder, `--dir` changes it; `--out .` from the project root, so the markup says `assets/img/photo--1200.webp`), and prints the `` or `` to paste; if the folder it prints differs, use that one. `credits` reads the page, so run it last, after the markup references the photographs: before that it exits 1 with "none of the fetched photographs is on the page". - `--trade`: cafe, bakery, hotel, bike (--shop only), food, florist, workshop, studio, office, shop, books, outdoors, wellness, farm, wine, bar; a brief's word works (roastery, bread, inn, bookshop, yoga studio, blacksmith). No trade for a restaurant, a ceramics studio, a patisserie, a salon, a jeweller, a goldsmith, a locksmith: its own photographs, else stand-ins from a live search (`search --trade restaurant`, the table above), else type. A **workshop** names its craft (`--trade blacksmith`, `weaving`, `letterpress`): only that craft's frames are dealt, so a smith's page never shows a weaver's loom; no craft named, nothing is dealt. - `--sections`: the page's sections in order, in plain words (bar, roastery, oven, dough, rooms, breakfast, workshop, stems...). Each gets a detail of its subject; a section the library cannot show comes back empty and goes to the client's own photograph, the object, UI or type. Repeat a word for a row (`rooms,rooms,rooms`: three details, one orientation). **Dealt nothing, on purpose:** hero (unless `--draft-lead`), menu, visit, contact, booking, closing and call to action, and, without `--own-land`, area, landscape, road, street and sky. - `--pictures N`: how many pictures the whole page carries, the client's own included (12 if not said). At most N/3 library frames are dealt, earlier sections first; the later ones come back empty and say so. With `--draft-lead` the cap lifts: every section that is not text gets a frame when the library has one. - Only photographs rated 7 or more, with no whole figure, no animal, no vehicle, no landmark and no mood frame (a curtain or plant shadows, a sky, fog, an aurora, a waterfall, a viewpoint), are dealt. A frame the curators or this review held back (`weak`, with its reason in `photos.json`) is never dealt. - **The land is only ever the client's own.** Library land is a draft stand-in, dealt only for the region a `--place` or the `--brief` names (as the lead; `--own-land` adds the land sections). A photograph's source names its places, the most exact first (Westfjords, Iceland), and a frame is dealt when its most exact name is the client's place, or the client's place is a broader one it lies in. `--place "Lofoten, Norway"` deals Lofoten; `--place Iceland` every photograph of Iceland; `--place "Reykjavik, Iceland"` neither the Westfjords nor a frame tagged only "Iceland" (a broader tag than the client's place is never dealt); names match whole, so "Senjavegen" is not Senja. Several places go in one value: `--place "Iceland; Norway; Faroe Islands"`. A place the source names overrides `--setting`; `--setting coast,mountain,...` only narrows frames whose source names no place, and never deals land by itself. With a `--place` and no photograph of it, the land sections stay empty. - Frames marked `moodOnly` (the file names a business, or it is another's named room) are never the client's room, counter or product: not the lead, not dealt to a trade that has its own premises (cafe, bakery, hotel, bar, bike, florist, workshop, food, shop, farm), and into a mood or interior section only for the rest. - `--draft-lead`: a lead may be dealt (a sharp landscape frame of the trade's lead subjects; a latte-art close-up or a soft, hazy older file never opens a page). A hero the library cannot fill comes back empty: never a row picture blown up. `--own-land`: see above. `--detail-only` is accepted and does nothing: it is the default. - `--commons-only`: Wikimedia Commons files only (the credit line then reads "Photographs via Wikimedia Commons"). - `--tone light|dark`, `--mono` (black and white, one deliberate frame), `--shop` (every make). - A place page's `pick` prints its hints for a place: words **under** the photograph on the ground, no band, no tab, no closing text. Product and service pages get the band and calm-side hints. - When `pick` says the library is short, run `photos.mjs search` (Live search above: CC0, CC BY, CC BY-SA, each looked at full size) before leaving the slot to the client's own or type. Detail frames held by default (`list` prints them live, after the full-size review that dropped 27 frames and merged 4; the 3 office rooms of the second merge were then set `weak`, as whole rooms; the third merge looked at 8 more at full size and kept none: a shopfront with its sign, two bars' counters and back bars, a breakfast room, a made-bed room, two breakfast tables rated below 7 and a half-eaten breakfast with a diner in the frame are all `weak`): cafe 19, bakery 4 (oven 3, dough 1), hotel 9 (7 details and 2 breakfast frames; its land only with `--own-land`), bike 6 (parts and a load, --shop only), workshop 5 (smith 4, instrument 1, weaving 0, letterpress 0: a craft is dealt only its own), studio 5, books 5 (desk only: a pencil on a notebook, a binding, stacked books, pencils; the hands frames beside a laptop are not dealt, and the bookbinder's gilding is dealt only to a bindery, `craft: bookbinding`), food 5, shop 3, florist 3, farm 3, wellness 3, office 3 (2 desk, 1 card), bar 0, outdoors 0 (land only), wine 0. A trade that holds 3 or fewer gives a page at most that many; the rest is the client's own. `list` marks those trades `thin`. - **Sections and subjects:** `hands`, `writing`, `notebook`, `paper` deal a hands or desk frame; `detail`, `texture`, `surface`, `linen`, `material` a detail, texture or desk frame; `breakfast` a hotel's breakfast frame (never a deli's); `rooms` a detail of a room, never the room.
